definition_zh: 糟糕地；差劲地；严重地；非常；处境困难
definition_en: in a poor or wrong way, severely, or very much
core_image: 一块歪掉的画框被越推越斜
scene: 墙上的画框本来就歪了，他又伸手推了一下，斜得更厉害。He hurt his knee badly when he fell off the bike.
sceneCN: 这里 badly 是「严重地」（第 2 个义项：程度很重）；句意为他从自行车上摔下来时膝盖伤得很重。

pos.zh: 副词：糟糕地；严重地；非常

derivatives.zh: 基础形容词，义为「坏的；有害的」
由 bad 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「坏；恶劣」
bad 的比较级，义为「更坏的」
bad 的最高级，义为「最坏的」

senses.title: In a poor way
senses.definition: in a way that is not good or not skillful
senses.definitionCN: 以不好或不熟练的方式
senses.example: She sings badly, but she never gives up.
senses.exampleCN: 她唱得不好，但从不放弃。
senses.why: Bad names what is not good, and the suffix -ly turns it into the manner of doing something, so doing a thing in a bad way is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: bad 指「不好」，后缀 -ly 把它变成做事情的方式，所以「以不好的方式做事」是最先长出的义项。

senses.title: Severely
senses.definition: to a serious or severe degree
senses.definitionCN: 达到严重或厉害的程度
senses.example: He cut his hand badly while cooking.
senses.exampleCN: 他做饭时把手割得很重。
senses.why: If an action goes in a bad direction, it can go far in that direction, and this gives the sense of severe degree.
senses.whyCN: 如果一件事朝坏的方向发展，就可能坏得很深，于是有了「程度严重」这个义项。

senses.title: Very much
senses.definition: very much, especially with need or want
senses.definitionCN: 非常，尤用于需要或想要
senses.example: I badly need a good sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 我非常需要好好睡一觉。
senses.why: Something that is badly needed is needed in a strong, almost painful degree, so the word came to mean simply very much.
senses.whyCN: 急需的东西，需要的程度又强又急，几乎带着痛感，于是这个词也引申为「非常」。

senses.title: Without success
senses.definition: to perform poorly in an exam, match, or competition
senses.definitionCN: 在考试、比赛或竞争中表现很差
senses.example: Our team did badly in the first half.
senses.exampleCN: 我们队上半场打得很差。
senses.why: Here the bad manner is measured by a result: the performance itself is the thing that turns out badly.
senses.whyCN: 这里「坏的方式」用结果来衡量：表现本身就是那个变坏的东西。

senses.title: In a bad position
senses.definition: in the phrase badly off, having very little money or few advantages
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 badly off，指钱很少或条件很差
senses.example: After the factory closed, many families were badly off.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂关闭后，许多家庭生活困难。
senses.why: The bad manner is now applied to a whole situation, so a person's circumstances themselves are in a bad state.
senses.whyCN: 「坏的方式」这时落到整个处境上，于是人的境况本身处于糟糕状态。

intro.en: Badly is a plain English adverb built from the adjective bad and an old suffix; the deeper origin of bad itself is uncertain.
intro.cn: badly 是地道的英语副词，由形容词 bad 加古老后缀构成；bad 本身更早的来源不确定。

items.en: A form badde is recorded in Old English, but its deeper origin is uncertain and different explanations exist.
items.cn: 古英语中记录有 badde 这一形式，但它更早的来源不确定，存在不同解释。

items.en: The adjective bad becomes common in Middle English, and the sources still do not agree on where it came from.
items.cn: 形容词 bad 在中古英语中变得常见，各家对它从何而来仍未取得一致。

items.en: The adverb suffix -ly goes back to Old English -lice, meaning in the manner of.
items.cn: 副词后缀 -ly 可追溯到古英语 -lice，意为「以……的方式」。

items.en: The adverb badly is recorded in Middle English; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 副词 badly 在中古英语中已有记录，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The sense very much, as in badly needed, grows later beside the older sense of severe degree.
items.cn: 「非常」这一义项，如 badly needed 中的用法，是较晚在「程度严重」之外发展出来的。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the bad family and the comparison forms; the near-meaning group gathers other adverbs that describe a poor or severe way.
note.cn: 形近组收 bad 这一词族与比较级形式；近义组收其他表示「差」或「严重」的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning not good, harmful, or serious.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「坏的、有害的、严重的」，是 badly 的基础词。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being bad.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「坏、恶劣」，由 bad 加 -ness 构成。

entries.definition: The comparative of bad, meaning more bad or more serious.
entries.definitionCN: bad 的比较级，义为「更坏的、更严重的」。

entries.definition: The superlative of bad, meaning the most bad.
entries.definitionCN: bad 的最高级，义为「最坏的」。

entries.definition: In a weak or unsatisfactory way; close to badly but more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「糟糕地、不佳地」，与 badly 接近但更正式。

entries.definition: In a very serious or harsh way; it matches the severe sense of badly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「严重地、严厉地」，对应 badly 的「严重」义项。

entries.definition: Very much; it matches the degree sense of badly without any bad meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「非常、大大地」，对应 badly 的程度义，但不带「坏」的色彩。

entries.definition: In a good or skillful way; the direct opposite of the first sense.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「好、很好地」，是第一个义项的直接反义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real pieces of the word: the adjective bad, the suffix -ly, and the irregular comparison worse and worst.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用这个词的真实构件：形容词 bad、后缀 -ly，以及不规则的比较级 worse 与最高级 worst。

normal.en: Bad plus -ly simply means in a bad way, just as quick plus -ly gives quickly.
normal.cn: bad 加 -ly 就是「以坏的方式」，正如 quick 加 -ly 成为 quickly。

normal.en: The comparison is irregular: bad, worse, worst, and badly follows the same pattern.
normal.cn: 比较级不规则：bad、worse、worst，badly 也沿用这一套。

normal.en: Badly hurt and badly damaged both show the sense of severe degree.
normal.cn: badly hurt 与 badly damaged 都体现「程度严重」这个义项。

normal.en: Badly needed means needed very much, not needed in a bad way.
normal.cn: badly needed 意为「非常需要」，不是「以坏的方式需要」。

normal.en: Badly off describes a person whose situation is poor, not an action done poorly.
normal.cn: badly off 描述的是人的境况差，而不是动作做得差。

abstract.en: Picture a crooked frame on the wall: every push makes it more crooked, and that is the direction the word points.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上一只歪画框：每推一下都更歪，这个词指的就是这个方向。

abstract.en: A badly tied knot comes apart, a badly hurt knee cannot bend, and the same word covers both.
abstract.cn: 系得很糟的结会散开，伤得很重的膝盖弯不了，同一个词把两件事都盖住了。

abstract.en: The word does not add a new idea; it only pushes the idea of bad into the verb or the situation.
abstract.cn: 这个词不增加新意思，只是把「坏」推进动作或处境里去。

examples.en: He hurt his knee badly when he fell off the bike.
examples.cn: 他从自行车上摔下来时膝盖伤得很重。

examples.en: The team played badly in the rain and lost the game.
examples.cn: 球队在雨中打得很差，输掉了比赛。

examples.en: I badly need a glass of water after the long run.
examples.cn: 长跑之后我非常需要一杯水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「掰得离」——一掰就坏，只好离远点：糟糕地、严重地

root: 由形容词 bad「坏的」加副词后缀 -ly 构成；-ly 来自古英语 -lice，意为「以……的方式」。bad 在古英语中已有 badde 形式，但更早词源存疑，各说不一。比较级 worse 与最高级 worst 为不规则形式。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of badly all push the idea of bad outward: into the manner of an action, the severity of damage, the strength of a need, the result of a performance, and the state of a whole situation.
sensesIntro.cn: badly 的五个义项都把「坏」向外推：推进动作的方式、伤害的程度、需要的强度、表现的结果，以及整个处境的状况。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a picture frame hangs crooked, and every touch pushes it further out of line.
core.cn: 核心意象：墙上的画框本就歪着，每碰一下都更偏离原位。

branches.en: THE MANNER: an action is done in a bad way, so the adverb first describes how.
branches.cn: 方式线：动作以坏的方式进行，所以副词最先描述「怎么做」。

branches.en: THE SEVERITY: the bad direction goes deep, and the word measures how serious the damage is.
branches.cn: 程度线：坏的方向走得很深，这个词就用来衡量伤害有多重。

branches.en: THE STRENGTH: a need felt this strongly becomes simply a very great need.
branches.cn: 强度线：被感受到如此强烈的需要，就变成了「非常」的需要。

branches.en: THE RESULT: when the manner is judged by an outcome, doing badly means failing to do well.
branches.cn: 结果线：当方式由结果来评判时，do badly 就是没能做好。

branches.en: THE SITUATION: the same bad state spreads from one action to a whole life, giving hardship.
branches.cn: 处境线：同样的坏状态从一个动作扩展到整个生活，就有了「生活困难」。

intro.en: Badly is a transparent English formation: a common adjective plus the adverb suffix -ly, with an irregular comparison.
intro.cn: badly 是结构透明的英语构词：常见形容词加副词后缀 -ly，比较级不规则。

latinIntro.en: Bad and its suffix belong to Germanic English; no Latin cognate is recorded, so the Latin list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: bad 及其后缀属于日耳曼语来源的英语，没有记录在案的拉丁同族词，因此拉丁词条留空。

items.example: The weather was bad all week.
items.exampleCN: 那一周天气一直很糟。

items.example: It turns bad into badly and quick into quickly.
items.exampleCN: 它把 bad 变成 badly，把 quick 变成 quickly。
球队打得很差。
它由 bad 构成 badness。

items.example: The second test was worse than the first.
items.exampleCN: 第二次测验比第一次更糟。

items.example: That was the worst day of the trip.
items.exampleCN: 那是旅行中最糟的一天。

items.example: The family was badly off that winter.
items.exampleCN: 那年冬天这家人生活困难。

items.example: The village received badly needed medicine.
items.exampleCN: 村子收到了急需的药品。

definition_zh: 袋子；包；手提包；一袋之量；眼袋
definition_en: a container made of soft material, used for carrying things
core_image: 一只敞口的布袋，袋口被拎在手里
scene: 超市收银台前，店员把苹果一个个装进纸袋。She put the apples in a paper bag and paid at the counter.
sceneCN: 这里 bag 是「袋子」（第 1 个义项：装东西的软质容器）；句意为她把苹果放进纸袋，然后在柜台付了钱。

pos.zh: 名词：袋子；包；手提包；一袋之量

derivatives.zh: 由 bag 加后缀 -ful 构成，义为「一满袋」
由 bag 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「宽松的、袋状的」
由 hand 与 bag 组合而成，义为「手提包」
经古法语进入英语，义为「行李」，与本词同源

senses.title: A soft container
senses.definition: a container made of paper, cloth, or plastic, used to hold and carry things
senses.definitionCN: 用纸、布或塑料制成、用来装东西和携带东西的容器
senses.example: She put the apples in a paper bag.
senses.exampleCN: 她把苹果放进纸袋里。
senses.why: The word first names the open soft container itself, because that is the object the root described.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最先指的是敞口软容器本身，因为词根描述的就是这件东西。

senses.title: A handbag
senses.definition: a bag with a handle, carried by a person, especially a woman's handbag
senses.definitionCN: 带提手、随身携带的包，尤指女式手提包
senses.example: He left his bag on the bus this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 今天早上他把包落在公交车上了。
senses.why: The container narrows to the one a person carries every day, so the general word becomes the everyday handbag.
senses.whyCN: 容器缩小到人每天随身带的那一只，于是泛称就变成了日常的「手提包」。

senses.title: The amount a bag holds
senses.definition: the quantity of something that fits in one bag
senses.definitionCN: 一只袋子能装下的数量
senses.example: We bought a bag of rice for the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 我们买了一袋米过冬。
senses.why: A container naturally measures what it holds, so the object also becomes a unit of quantity.
senses.whyCN: 容器天然可以衡量它所装的东西，于是这件东西也变成了计量单位。

senses.title: Loose skin under the eyes
senses.definition: small dark or swollen folds of skin under the eyes, often from tiredness
senses.definitionCN: 眼睛下方发暗或浮肿的小褶皱，常因疲劳出现
senses.example: Bags under his eyes showed that he had not slept.
senses.exampleCN: 他眼下的眼袋说明他没有睡好。
senses.why: The loose fold of skin hangs like a small pouch, so the container image is applied to the body.
senses.whyCN: 松垂的皮肤像一只小口袋挂着，于是容器的意象被用到身体上。

senses.title: To put into a bag or take
senses.definition: to put something into a bag, or to take and keep something for oneself
senses.definitionCN: 把东西装进袋子，或把某物拿走据为己有
senses.example: The clerk bagged the groceries in a few seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 店员几秒钟就把食品装好了袋。
senses.why: The verb turns the container into the action of filling it; from taking things into a bag comes the sense of taking for oneself.
senses.whyCN: 动词把容器变成「装满」的动作；从把东西收进袋子，又引申出「据为己有」。

intro.en: Bag is a Germanic word recorded in Middle English; its deeper origin is not fully certain.
intro.cn: bag 是记录于中古英语的日耳曼语词，更早的来源并不完全确定。

items.en: It is generally thought to come from Old Norse baggi, meaning a bag or bundle, though the origin is not fully certain.
items.cn: 一般认为它来自古诺尔斯语 baggi，意为「袋子、包裹」，但来源并不完全确定。

items.en: Related words for a sack appear in other Germanic languages, which supports a Germanic source.
items.cn: 其他日耳曼语中也有表示「袋子」的相关词，这支持它源于日耳曼语。

items.en: The word appears in Middle English as bagge, naming a sack or pouch.
items.cn: 这个词在中古英语中写作 bagge，指袋子或小包。

items.en: The handbag and the bags under the eyes are later extensions of the same container image.
items.cn: 手提包与眼袋都是同一容器意象后来扩展出的用法。

items.en: The verb to bag, meaning to put into a bag or to seize, develops from the noun.
items.cn: 动词 bag 表示「装袋」或「占取」，是由名词发展出来的。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on bag or sharing its shape; the near-meaning group gathers other containers for carrying things.
note.cn: 形近组收由 bag 构成或拼写相近的词；近义组收其他用来装带物品的容器。

entries.definition: The amount that fills one bag.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一满袋」，由 bag 加 -ful 构成。

entries.definition: Loose and hanging like a bag, used of clothes.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「宽松的、袋状的」，多形容衣服，由 bag 加 -y 构成。

entries.definition: A small bag carried by hand, usually by a woman.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「手提包」，由 hand 与 bag 组合而成。

entries.definition: Luggage; it came through Old French and is related to bag.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「行李」，经古法语进入英语，与 bag 同源。

entries.definition: A large strong bag for grain or potatoes; bigger and rougher than a bag.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「麻袋、大袋」，装粮食或土豆，比 bag 更大更粗。

entries.definition: A small soft bag, often closed with a drawstring.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小袋、荷包」，常用绳子收口。

entries.definition: A stiff case with a handle, used for clothes when travelling.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「行李箱」，硬质带提手，旅行时装衣物。

entries.definition: A bag carried on the back with two straps.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「双肩背包」，用两条背带背在背上。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real pieces of the family: the root bag, the suffixes -ful, -y and -age, and common compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用这一词族的真实构件：词根 bag，后缀 -ful、-y、-age，以及常见复合词。

normal.en: A bagful is exactly what one bag can hold, so -ful turns the container into a quantity.
normal.cn: bagful 正是一只袋子能装下的量，-ful 把容器变成数量。

normal.en: Baggy trousers hang loosely like a bag, which is why -y adds the idea of a bag shape.
normal.cn: baggy 的裤子松松垮垮像袋子，所以 -y 加上的是「袋状」的意思。

normal.en: A handbag is a bag carried by hand; the compound simply names how it is carried.
normal.cn: handbag 是用手提的包，复合词只是说明携带方式。

normal.en: Bags under the eyes look like two small pouches hanging below the eyelids.
normal.cn: 眼袋就像挂在眼皮下面的两只小口袋。

normal.en: Pack your bags uses the plural because a trip needs more than one container.
normal.cn: pack your bags 用复数，因为出门往往不止一只包。

abstract.en: Picture an open cloth bag: anything dropped in stays together, and that is the whole idea of the word.
abstract.cn: 想象一只敞口布袋：放进去的东西都被收在一起，这就是这个词的全部意思。

abstract.en: The same shape moves from shopping to the shoulder to the skin under the eyes, always a soft holder.
abstract.cn: 同一个形状从购物袋移到肩上，再移到眼下皮肤，始终是一个柔软的盛放物。

abstract.en: To bag something is to close the bag on it, which is why the verb can also mean to take it.
abstract.cn: 把东西 bag 起来就是把袋口在它上面合上，所以动词也能表示「把它拿走」。

examples.en: She put the apples in a paper bag and paid at the counter.
examples.cn: 她把苹果放进纸袋，然后在柜台付了钱。

examples.en: He left his bag on the bus this morning.
examples.cn: 今天早上他把包落在公交车上了。

examples.en: We bought a bag of rice for the winter.
examples.cn: 我们买了一袋米过冬。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「白哥」——白哥背着一只白布袋去买米：袋子、包

root: bag 为日耳曼语来源，一般认为借自古诺尔斯语 baggi「袋子、包裹」，更早词源不完全确定。英语中由它构成 bagful、baggy、handbag 等词；baggage 经古法语 bagage 进入英语，与 bag 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of bag all keep one soft container in view: the container itself, the everyday handbag, the quantity it holds, the pouch of skin under the eye, and the act of filling or taking.
sensesIntro.cn: bag 的五个义项都围绕同一只软容器：容器本身、日常手提包、它装下的数量、眼下的皮袋，以及装袋或占取的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open cloth bag is held by its neck, ready to receive whatever is dropped in.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只敞口布袋被人拎着袋口，随时接住放进去的东西。

branches.en: THE CONTAINER: the word starts as the soft holder itself, made of paper, cloth, or plastic.
branches.cn: 容器线：这个词最初就是那只软质盛放物，用纸、布或塑料制成。

branches.en: THE CARRY: a bag with a handle becomes the one a person takes everywhere.
branches.cn: 携带线：带提手的袋子变成人随身携带的那一只。

branches.en: THE QUANTITY: what one bag holds becomes a unit of measure.
branches.cn: 数量线：一只袋子所装的量变成了计量单位。

branches.en: THE BODY: a loose fold of skin under the eye hangs like a small pouch.
branches.cn: 身体线：眼下松垂的一小片皮肤像小口袋一样挂着。

branches.en: THE ACTION: filling the bag, and then taking what is in it, gives the verb its two shades.
branches.cn: 动作线：把东西装进袋子，再把袋里的东西拿走，给了动词两层意思。

intro.en: Bag is a short Germanic root that forms a small family with English suffixes and compounding.
intro.cn: bag 是简短的日耳曼语词根，靠英语后缀与复合构词形成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Bag has no recorded Latin cognate, so the Latin list is empty; the related baggage came through French instead.
latinIntro.cn: bag 没有记录在案的拉丁同族词，所以拉丁词条留空；相关的 baggage 是经法语传来的。

items.example: The bag was full of apples.
items.exampleCN: 袋子里装满了苹果。
它由 bag 构成 bagful。
它由 bag 构成 baggy。
它与 bag 构成 handbag。

items.example: It forms school bag with bag.

它由 bag 构成 bags。

definition_zh: 平衡；余额；天平；剩余部分；使平衡；权衡
definition_en: an even state in which nothing falls or is heavier, or the money left in an account
core_image: 一架天平两端各放一枚砝码，横梁停在水平
scene: 窄墙上，她张开双臂，慢慢把身体稳住。She held out her arms to keep her balance on the narrow wall.
sceneCN: 这里 balance 是「平衡」（第 1 个义项：身体不倾倒的均衡状态）；句意为她张开双臂，在窄墙上保持平衡。

pos.zh: 名词：平衡；余额；天平；剩余部分

derivatives.zh: 由 balance 加 -ed 构成，义为「均衡的、平稳的」
由否定前缀 im- 与 balance 构成，义为「失衡」
由否定前缀 un- 与 balanced 构成，义为「不平衡的；失常的」
由 counter-「对抗」与 balance 构成，义为「抗衡物、平衡力」

senses.title: An even state
senses.definition: a steady state in which weight or force is even and nothing falls
senses.definitionCN: 重量或力量均匀、不会倒下的稳定状态
senses.example: She held out her arms to keep her balance.
senses.exampleCN: 她张开双臂保持平衡。
senses.why: The Latin word named a pair of scales with two equal pans, so the first sense is the even state of the beam.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词本指两盘相等的一架天平，所以第一个义项就是横梁持平的均衡状态。

senses.title: Money left in an account
senses.definition: the amount of money remaining in a bank account after payments
senses.definitionCN: 银行账户在支付之后剩余的金额
senses.example: He checked his bank balance before buying the ticket.
senses.exampleCN: 买票之前他查了账户余额。
senses.why: Money in and money out are weighed like two pans; what is left when they even out is the balance.
senses.whyCN: 进账与出账像两只秤盘一样被称量，两者相抵后剩下的就是 balance。

senses.title: A weighing device
senses.definition: a device with two pans for weighing things by comparing weights
senses.definitionCN: 有两个秤盘、通过比较重量来称物的器具
senses.example: The old balance stood on the shop counter.
senses.exampleCN: 那架旧天平摆在商店柜台上。
senses.why: This is the original object itself: the instrument whose two pans must come level.
senses.whyCN: 这是最初的那件器物本身：两只秤盘必须保持水平的天平。

senses.title: The rest of something
senses.definition: the part of something that remains after the other parts are used
senses.definitionCN: 其他部分用掉之后剩下的那部分
senses.example: The balance of the money went to the school.
senses.exampleCN: 剩下的钱给了学校。
senses.why: Once one side of an account is settled, what is left over is what keeps the two sides level, so the remainder is also the balance.
senses.whyCN: 账目的一边结清后，剩下用来让两边持平的部分就是余额，于是「剩余部分」也叫 balance。

senses.title: To keep steady
senses.definition: to keep something in a steady position so that it does not fall
senses.definitionCN: 使某物保持稳定位置而不倒下
senses.example: He balanced the box on one hand.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一只手把箱子端平。
senses.why: The verb turns the even state into an action: holding the object so that the two sides stay level.
senses.whyCN: 动词把均衡状态变成动作：扶住物体，让两边保持水平。

senses.title: To weigh two things against each other
senses.definition: to compare two needs or choices and give each a fair share of attention
senses.definitionCN: 比较两种需要或选择，并各给适当的重视
senses.example: She balanced study and sport every week.
senses.exampleCN: 她每周都兼顾学习与运动。
senses.why: When the two pans hold different things, the mind weighs them; giving each its fair weight is the abstract sense.
senses.whyCN: 当两只秤盘装着不同的东西时，人会在心里称量；给每一方适当的重量，就是抽象的「权衡」。

intro.en: Balance goes back to a Latin name for a two-pan scale and reached English through French.
intro.cn: balance 可追溯到拉丁语中「双盘天平」的名称，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Lanx was the Latin word for a flat dish or the pan of a scale; its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: lanx 是拉丁语「浅盘、秤盘」，更早来源不确定。

items.en: The prefix bi- meaning two plus lanx formed bilanx, describing a scale with two pans.
items.cn: 表示「二」的前缀 bi- 加 lanx 构成 bilanx，指有两隻秤盘的天平。

items.en: Old French balance carried both the instrument and the idea of an even state into English.
items.cn: 古法语 balance 把「天平」这件器具与「均衡」的观念一起带入英语。

items.en: Middle English used the word for scales and for the even state of anything weighed.
items.cn: 中古英语用这个词指天平，也指被称量之物的均衡状态。

items.en: The financial sense of the money left in an account develops from the image of two sides that must come level.
items.cn: 账户余额这一财务义项，是从「两边必须持平」的意象发展出来的。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on balance or sharing its Latin pieces; the near-meaning group gathers words for steadiness, weighing, and what is left over.
note.cn: 形近组收由 balance 构成或共享拉丁构件的词；近义组收表示稳定、称量与剩余的词。

entries.definition: Adjective meaning steady, even, or giving fair weight to each side.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「均衡的、平稳的」，由 balance 加 -ed 构成。

entries.definition: A state in which one side is heavier or stronger than the other.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「失衡」，指一方比另一方更重或更强。

entries.definition: A weight or force that balances another one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「抗衡物、平衡力」，指抵消另一方重量的东西。

entries.definition: A small platform outside a window; it only looks similar and comes from a different Italian word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「阳台」；只是拼写与发音相近，词源不同，来自意大利语而非天平。

entries.definition: A state of perfect balance between opposing forces; more technical than balance.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「平衡、均衡」，指对立力量之间的完美均势，比 balance 更专业。

entries.definition: The quality of being firm and not shaking; it stresses the result rather than the weighing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「稳定、平稳」，强调不晃动的结果，而不含称量的意味。

entries.definition: The part that is left over; it matches the fourth sense without the scale image.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「剩余部分」，对应第四个义项，但不带天平的意象。

entries.definition: A device for weighing; the everyday word for the third sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「秤、天平」，是第三个义项的日常说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin pieces bi- and lanx, the suffix -ance, and the everyday phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁构件 bi- 与 lanx、后缀 -ance，以及这个词实际出现的日常搭配。

normal.en: Bilanx means two pans: bi- is two, lanx is a pan, and a balance is the beam that keeps them level.
normal.cn: bilanx 意为「两只秤盘」：bi- 是二，lanx 是盘，balance 就是让两盘持平的横梁。

normal.en: The noun suffix -ance names a state, so balance is the state of being level.
normal.cn: 名词后缀 -ance 表示状态，所以 balance 就是「处于水平」的状态。

normal.en: Keep your balance and lose your balance are the two daily phrases about the body.
normal.cn: keep your balance 与 lose your balance 是日常谈身体平衡的两个固定说法。

normal.en: A bank balance is the money that keeps the two sides of an account level.
normal.cn: bank balance 就是让账户两边持平的那笔钱。

normal.en: Balance the budget means making income and spending weigh the same.
normal.cn: balance the budget 意为让收入与支出称起来一样重。

abstract.en: Picture a beam with one coin on each pan: the moment it stops moving is the moment the word describes.
abstract.cn: 想象横梁两端各放一枚硬币：它停止晃动的那一刻，正是这个词描述的状态。

abstract.en: The same beam can hold money instead of coins, and then the balance is what is left in the account.
abstract.cn: 同一根横梁上也可以放钱而不是硬币，这时 balance 就是账户里剩下的数目。

abstract.en: When two duties sit on the pans, keeping the beam level is not a physical act but a choice.
abstract.cn: 当两只秤盘上放着两份责任时，让横梁保持水平不再是体力动作，而是一种选择。

examples.en: She held out her arms to keep her balance on the narrow wall.
examples.cn: 她张开双臂，在窄墙上保持平衡。

examples.en: He checked his bank balance before buying the ticket.
examples.cn: 买票之前他查了账户余额。

examples.en: A good student balances study and rest.
examples.cn: 好学生懂得兼顾学习与休息。

root: 拉丁语 bilanx「双盘天平」由 bi-「二」+ lanx「秤盘、浅盘」构成，lanx 更早来源不确定；经古法语 balance 进入英语。由「天平持平」引申出「余额、剩余部分、权衡」等义。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses of balance all come from one beam with two pans: the even state, the money that keeps an account level, the instrument itself, what is left over, the act of holding something steady, and the mental act of weighing two needs.
sensesIntro.cn: balance 的六个义项都来自一根架着两盘的横梁：均衡状态、让账户持平的余额、天平本身、剩余部分、扶稳物体的动作，以及心里权衡两种需要。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a beam with a pan on each side stops moving and rests exactly level.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根两端各挂一只秤盘的横梁停止晃动，正好停在水平位置。

branches.en: THE STATE: two equal weights leave the beam level, and that even state is the first sense.
branches.cn: 状态线：两份相等的重量让横梁持平，这个均衡状态就是第一义。

branches.en: THE ACCOUNT: money in and money out are weighed, and what keeps the two sides level is the balance.
branches.cn: 账目线：进账与出账被称量，让两边持平的那部分就是余额。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT: before it was an idea, balance was the physical scale on the counter.
branches.cn: 器物线：在成为观念之前，balance 就是柜台上那架实体天平。

branches.en: THE ACTION: the verb holds an object so that it does not tip.
branches.cn: 动作线：动词指扶住物体，使它不倾倒。

branches.en: THE MIND: two duties sit on the pans, and balancing them becomes a fair judgment.
branches.cn: 心智线：两份责任放在秤盘上，让它们平衡就成了一种公正的判断。

intro.en: Balance is built from a Latin prefix and a Latin noun, then enlarged by English suffixes and a combining prefix.

latinIntro.en: Latin lanx and bilanx are recorded, so only the deeper origin of lanx is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 lanx 与 bilanx 均有文献记录，只有 lanx 更早的来源不确定。

definition_zh: 球；球类运动；舞会；一团（线等）
definition_en: a round object that is thrown, kicked, or hit in games
core_image: 一只圆球在草地上弹了两下，滚到脚边
scene: 操场上，男孩一脚把球踢进球门。The boy kicked the ball into the goal.
sceneCN: 这里 ball 是「球」（第 1 个义项：圆形的球体）；句意为男孩一脚把球踢进了球门。

pos.zh: 名词：球；球类运动；舞会；一团

由 foot 与 ball 组合而成，义为「足球」
由 volley 与 ball 组合而成，义为「排球」
由 snow 与 ball 组合而成，义为「雪球」

senses.title: A round object
senses.definition: a round object that rolls and is used in games
senses.definitionCN: 会滚动、用于游戏的圆形物体
senses.example: The boy kicked the ball into the goal.
senses.exampleCN: 男孩一脚把球踢进了球门。
senses.why: The Germanic source named a round swelling thing, so the concrete round object is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 它的日耳曼语来源本指圆而鼓起的物体，所以具体的圆形球体是第一义。

senses.title: A game played with a ball
senses.definition: a game or sport in which a ball is thrown, kicked, or hit
senses.definitionCN: 以投、踢或击球进行的游戏或运动
senses.example: The children play ball in the park every Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们每周日在公园里打球。
senses.why: Because the object is central to the game, the object's name comes to stand for the whole activity.
senses.whyCN: 因为球是这项活动的核心，球的名字就用来指整项运动。

senses.title: A formal dance
senses.definition: a large formal party where people dance
senses.definitionCN: 人们跳舞的大型正式聚会
senses.example: They met at a school ball last winter.
senses.exampleCN: 他们去年冬天在一场学校舞会上相识。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different source, the Latin verb for dancing, and simply shares the modern spelling.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项另有来源，来自表示「跳舞」的拉丁动词，只是与现代拼写相同。

senses.title: A round mass
senses.definition: something soft pressed or wound into a round shape
senses.definitionCN: 柔软之物被压成或绕成的圆团
senses.example: She rolled the wool into a ball.
senses.exampleCN: 她把毛线绕成了一团。
senses.why: Anything gathered into the same round shape can take the name, even when it is not used for play.
senses.whyCN: 任何被收拢成同样圆形的柔软之物都能叫这个名字，即使不用于游戏。

intro.en: Ball has two histories: the round object is Germanic, while the dance sense came through French from Latin.
intro.cn: ball 有两条历史：表示圆球的义项来自日耳曼语，表示舞会的义项则经法语来自拉丁语。

items.en: A reconstructed Germanic form names a round, swelling object; the deeper Indo-European link is uncertain.
items.cn: 可重构的日耳曼语形式指「圆而鼓起的物体」，更早的印欧语联系不确定。

items.en: Old Norse bollr, meaning a round object, is generally taken as the source of the English word.
items.cn: 一般认为古诺尔斯语 bollr「圆形物」是英语这个词的来源。

items.en: Middle English bal names a round object used in games.
items.cn: 中古英语 bal 指游戏中使用的圆形物体。

items.en: The dance sense comes separately through Old French baller, to dance, from Late Latin ballare.
items.cn: 「舞会」义另外经古法语 baller「跳舞」而来，其源头是晚期拉丁语 ballare。

items.en: The two words now look and sound the same, but their histories remain separate.
items.cn: 这两个词现在拼写与读音相同，但各自的历史仍然是分开的。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds formed with ball; the near-meaning group gathers other round objects and games.
note.cn: 形近组收由 ball 构成的复合词；近义组收其他圆形物体与球类活动。

entries.definition: A game in which a ball is thrown through a high hoop, or the ball used.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「篮球运动、篮球」，由 basket 与 ball 组合而成。

entries.definition: A game played by kicking a ball, or the ball itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「足球、足球运动」，由 foot 与 ball 组合而成。

entries.definition: A game in which players hit a ball over a net with their hands.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「排球」，由 volley 与 ball 组合而成。

entries.definition: A ball made of snow pressed together.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「雪球」，由 snow 与 ball 组合而成。

entries.definition: A perfectly round solid shape; the geometric word for a ball.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「球体」，是 ball 的几何学说法。

entries.definition: A round model of the earth, or any round object.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「地球仪、球状物」，强调浑圆的外形。

entries.definition: A social event where people move to music; it matches the third sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「舞会、跳舞」，对应第三个义项。

entries.definition: A sports game between two sides; it matches the second sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「比赛」，对应第二个义项，但不限于球类。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real compounds of ball and the everyday phrases it appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用 ball 的真实复合词，以及它实际出现的日常搭配。

normal.en: Basket plus ball and foot plus ball show how the game is named after what is kicked or thrown.
normal.cn: basket 加 ball、foot 加 ball 说明运动是按被投或被踢的那个球来命名的。

normal.en: A ball of string keeps the same round shape as a ball on the field.
normal.cn: 一团毛线保持着和球场上那只球同样的圆形。

normal.en: Play ball began as a call to start the game, and now it means to get going.
normal.cn: play ball 最初是宣布开赛的喊声，现在也表示「开始行动」。

normal.en: Have a ball means to enjoy yourself, as if the whole evening were a dance.
normal.cn: have a ball 意为玩得尽兴，仿佛整晚都是舞会。

normal.en: The ball is in your court comes from tennis: it is your turn to act.
normal.cn: 「the ball is in your court」来自网球：球在你这边，该你行动了。

abstract.en: Picture a round stone rolling down a hill: it keeps turning but stays one shape, which is the core of the word.
abstract.cn: 想象一块圆石从山坡滚下：它一直转，却始终是一个形状，这就是这个词的核心。

abstract.en: The same round shape can be wool, snow, or a planet seen from far away.
abstract.cn: 同一个圆形可以是毛线团、雪球，也可以是远处看到的一颗行星。

abstract.en: A dance and a football seem unrelated, yet English gave them one spelling by accident of history.
abstract.cn: 舞会和足球看似无关，英语却因历史的巧合让它们共用一个拼写。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of ball keep one round shape in view: the object used in games, the game itself, a formal dance that merely shares the spelling, and any soft mass wound into a round form.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round object lands, bounces twice, and rolls to a stop at your foot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只圆球落地，弹了两下，滚到你脚边停住。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the first sense is simply the round thing that rolls.
branches.cn: 物体线：第一义就是那只会滚动的圆形物。

branches.en: THE GAME: because the object is central, its name stands for the whole sport.
branches.cn: 运动线：因为球是核心，球的名字就代表整项运动。

branches.en: THE SHAPE: anything soft wound into the same round form borrows the name.
branches.cn: 形状线：任何被绕成同样圆形的柔软之物都借用了这个名字。

branches.en: THE DANCE: a separate French word for dancing happens to share the modern spelling.
branches.cn: 舞会线：另一个来自法语的「跳舞」词恰好与现代拼写相同。

branches.en: THE FIELD: object and game sit together in phrases such as kick a ball and play ball.
branches.cn: 球场线：物体与运动在 kick a ball、play ball 这类说法里并置。

intro.en: Ball forms most of its family by compounding, with the round object as the second element.
intro.cn: ball 的词族主要靠复合构词形成，圆球义常作为第二个成分。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb ballare is recorded for the dance sense; the round-object word has no Latin cognate.
latinIntro.cn: 表示舞会的义项有文献记录的拉丁动词 ballare；表示圆球的词则没有拉丁同族词。

definition_zh: 香蕉；香蕉树；发疯（用于口语短语）
definition_en: a long curved fruit with a yellow skin and soft white flesh
core_image: 一只弯弯的黄香蕉被剥开一半
scene: 早餐桌上，孩子剥开一根香蕉，三口就吃完了。He peeled a banana and ate it before school.
sceneCN: 这里 banana 是「香蕉」（第 1 个义项：这种弯曲的黄色果实）；句意为他在上学前剥了一根香蕉吃。

derivatives.zh: 由 banana 加复数词尾构成的口语形容词，义为「发疯的」
由 banana 与 bread 组合而成，义为「香蕉面包」

senses.title: The fruit
senses.definition: a long curved fruit with yellow skin and soft white flesh, growing in bunches
senses.definitionCN: 成串生长、有黄色外皮和柔软白色果肉的长弯形果实
senses.example: He peeled a banana and ate it before school.
senses.exampleCN: 他在上学前剥了一根香蕉吃。
senses.why: The word entered English with the fruit itself, so the fruit is the first and central sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是随着果实一起进入英语的，所以果实是第一义，也是中心义。

senses.title: The plant
senses.definition: the tall tropical plant with large leaves that produces bananas
senses.definitionCN: 结出香蕉、叶片宽大的高大热带植物
senses.example: Banana plants need plenty of water and sun.
senses.exampleCN: 香蕉树需要充足的水分和阳光。
senses.why: Because the plant exists mainly for its fruit, the fruit's name is simply extended to the whole plant.
senses.whyCN: 因为这种植物主要因果实而被栽培，果实的名字就直接扩展到了整株植物。

senses.title: Crazy, in the phrase go bananas
senses.definition: in the informal phrase go bananas, to become very excited, angry, or crazy
senses.definitionCN: 用于口语短语 go bananas，指变得非常激动、生气或失去理智
senses.example: The crowd went bananas when the team scored.
senses.exampleCN: 球队得分时，人群都疯了似的欢呼。
senses.why: The fruit is bent and wild in shape, and the informal image of going bananas borrows that wildness for wild behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 香蕉形状弯而野，口语里 go bananas 就借这种「野」来形容失控的行为。

intro.en: Banana came into English from the Atlantic trade and is ultimately traced to West Africa.
intro.cn: banana 经大西洋贸易进入英语，最终一般追溯到西非语言。

items.en: The word is generally traced to a West African language, often cited as Wolof or Mandinka, though the exact source is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词一般被追溯到某种西非语言，常被举为沃洛夫语或曼丁哥语，但确切来源不确定。

items.en: Portuguese and Spanish traders used banana for the fruit in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 十六世纪时，葡萄牙与西班牙商人已用 banana 指这种水果。

items.en: English borrowed the word along with the fruit; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语随着果实一起借入了这个词，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The same word also names the tall plant that bears the fruit.
items.cn: 同一个词也用来指结出果实的那种高大植物。

items.en: Informal phrases such as go bananas extend the word far beyond the fruit.
items.cn: go bananas 这类口语说法把这个词远远扩展到果实之外。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds and forms built on banana; the near-meaning group gathers other tropical fruits and the plant name.
note.cn: 形近组收由 banana 构成的复合词与形式；近义组收其他热带水果及植物名称。

entries.definition: An informal adjective meaning crazy or very excited.
entries.definitionCN: 口语形容词，义为「发疯的、极度兴奋的」，由 banana 加复数词尾而来。

entries.definition: The skin of a banana, often used in jokes about slipping.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「香蕉皮」，常出现在滑倒的笑话里。

entries.definition: A sweet bread made with mashed bananas.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「香蕉面包」，用捣碎的香蕉制成。

entries.definition: A starchy cooking banana; the word looks unrelated and comes from a different source.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大蕉」，是可烹食的香蕉近亲；拼写与 banana 不同，词源也另有所出。

entries.definition: The general word for the sweet part of a plant that holds seeds.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「水果」，是这类可食果实的总称。

entries.definition: A sweet tropical fruit with yellow flesh; another fruit carried into English by trade.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「芒果」，另一种经贸易传入英语的热带水果。

entries.definition: A group of fruits growing or held together, as in a bunch of bananas.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「串、束」，如 a bunch of bananas 中的用法。

entries.definition: The skin of a fruit, or to remove that skin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「果皮；剥皮」，常与香蕉等水果搭配。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real shape of the word, its plural form, and the compounds and phrases it appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用这个词的真实形状、复数形式，以及它出现的复合词和短语。

normal.en: A bunch of bananas hangs together, which is why the fruit is usually counted by the bunch.
normal.cn: 一串香蕉总是挂在一起，所以这种水果常按「串」来计数。

normal.en: Banana peel is the skin, and banana bread is the fruit baked into bread.
normal.cn: banana peel 是果皮，banana bread 是把果肉烘进面包里。

normal.en: The plant and the fruit share one name because the plant is grown for the fruit.
normal.cn: 植物与果实共用一个名字，因为种这种植物就是为了果实。

normal.en: Go bananas is informal and means to lose control, not to eat fruit.
normal.cn: go bananas 是口语，意为失控，不是去吃水果。

normal.en: The plural bananas also works as an adjective, as in the crowd went bananas.
normal.cn: 复数形式 bananas 也能当形容词用，如人群 went bananas。

abstract.en: Picture a yellow curve: the shape is so distinctive that the whole plant takes its name from it.
abstract.cn: 想象一道黄色的弧线：这个形状太鲜明，整株植物都跟着叫这个名字。

abstract.en: A fruit that arrives by ship carries its foreign name with it, which is how the word entered English.
abstract.cn: 随船而来的水果把外来的名字也带了过来，这个词就是这样进入英语的。

abstract.en: The same word can name a fruit, a plant, and a wild mood, because languages reuse what is familiar.
abstract.cn: 同一个词可以指果实、植物和失控的情绪，因为语言总是复用熟悉的东西。

examples.cn: 她在市场上买了一串香蕉。

examples.en: The crowd went bananas when the team scored.

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of banana move outward from the fruit: the fruit itself, the plant grown for it, and an informal phrase for wild behaviour.
sensesIntro.cn: banana 的三个义项从果实向外扩展：果实本身、为结果实而种植的植物，以及形容失控行为的口语短语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long yellow fruit curves in the hand, its skin half opened.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根长长的黄色果实弯在手里，外皮剥开了一半。

branches.en: THE FRUIT: the word arrived with the fruit, so the fruit is the centre of the map.
branches.cn: 果实线：这个词随果实一起传来，所以果实是这张图的中心。

branches.en: THE PLANT: the tall tropical plant takes the fruit's name because it is grown for it.
branches.cn: 植物线：高大的热带植物因专为结果而种，便借用了果实的名字。

branches.en: THE MOOD: go bananas borrows the fruit's wild curve for wild behaviour.
branches.cn: 情绪线：go bananas 借果实弯曲不羁的形状来形容失控的行为。

branches.en: THE BUNCH: bananas grow in bunches, and that is how they are counted and sold.
branches.cn: 成串线：香蕉成串生长，也因此按串计数和出售。

branches.en: THE TROPICS: the plant needs heat and water, which ties the word to warm regions.
branches.cn: 热带线：这种植物需要高温与水分，把这词与温暖地区连在一起。

intro.en: Banana is a borrowed root; English builds its compounds by putting the fruit word first.
intro.cn: banana 是借入的词根，英语把它放在前面来构成复合词。

latinIntro.en: The word comes from West African languages through Portuguese and Spanish, so no Latin cognate is recorded and the list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词经葡萄牙语与西班牙语来自西非语言，没有记录在案的拉丁同族词，因此列表留空。

definition_zh: 乐队；带子；波段；一伙人；用带子绑；联合
definition_en: a group of musicians, or a thin flat strip used to tie or fasten things
core_image: 一条布带把一捆木棍紧紧束在一起
scene: 学校礼堂里，乐队奏响了第一首歌，台下立刻安静下来。The band played three songs at the school concert.
sceneCN: 这里 band 是「乐队」（第 1 个义项：一起演奏的一群音乐人）；句意为乐队在学校音乐会上演奏了三首歌。

pos.zh: 名词：乐队；带子；波段；一伙人

derivatives.zh: 由 head 与 band 组合而成，义为「发带、头带」
由 waist 与 band 组合而成，义为「腰带、腰头」
由 band 与 width 组合而成，义为「带宽」
由 band 与 stand 组合而成，义为「露天音乐台」

senses.title: A group of musicians
senses.definition: a small group of people who play music together
senses.definitionCN: 一起演奏音乐的一小群人
senses.example: The band played three songs at the school concert.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队在学校音乐会上演奏了三首歌。
senses.why: A band first meant a company of people bound together, so a group of musicians bound by playing is a natural extension.
senses.whyCN: band 本指被束在一起的一伙人，所以因演奏而聚在一起的一群音乐人是很自然的引申。

senses.title: A thin strip
senses.definition: a thin flat strip of material used to tie, fasten, or decorate something
senses.definitionCN: 用来捆扎、固定或装饰的细长扁条
senses.example: He tied the pencils with a rubber band.
senses.exampleCN: 他用橡皮筋把铅笔捆在一起。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the physical strip that binds things, and that image lies under all the others.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是那条把东西束起来的实物流，它下面的所有义项都从这一形象长出。

senses.title: A range of radio waves
senses.definition: a particular range of frequencies used for radio or other signals
senses.definitionCN: 用于无线电或其他信号的特定频率范围
senses.example: This radio can receive the short-wave band.
senses.exampleCN: 这台收音机能接收短波波段。
senses.why: A strip of the frequency scale is imagined as a strip of material, so a range of waves becomes a band.
senses.whyCN: 频率刻度上的一段被想象成一条带子，于是一段波的范围也叫 band。

senses.title: A group of people
senses.definition: a group of people who share an activity, sometimes with a bad purpose
senses.definitionCN: 因共同活动聚在一起的一群人，有时带贬义
senses.example: A band of thieves broke into the shop at night.
senses.exampleCN: 一伙盗贼夜里闯进了商店。
senses.why: People tied by a common purpose are like things tied by a strip, which gives the group sense.
senses.whyCN: 被共同目的束在一起的人，就像被带子捆住的物件，于是有了「一伙人」的义项。

senses.title: To tie or unite
senses.definition: to fasten something with a band, or to join together for a common aim
senses.definitionCN: 用带子捆住某物，或为共同目标联合起来
senses.example: The villagers banded together to repair the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们联合起来修桥。
senses.why: The verb is the strip in action: putting the band around something, or making a group into one bound unit.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是那条带子在起作用：把带子绕上去，或把一群人束成一个整体。

intro.en: Band comes from a Germanic root meaning to bind, and entered English through both Norse and French.
intro.cn: band 来自表示「捆绑」的日耳曼语词根，经诺尔斯语与法语两条路径进入英语。

items.en: The Germanic verb meaning to bind is the distant root of the word.
items.cn: 表示「捆绑」的日耳曼语动词是这个词的远源。

items.en: Old Norse band meant a cord or a band that fastens something.
items.cn: 古诺尔斯语 band 指用来捆扎的绳或带。

items.en: Old French bande meant a strip and also a troop of people, and reinforced both senses in English.
items.cn: 古法语 bande 既指带子，也指一队人，这两个义项都强化了英语中的用法。

items.en: Middle English used band for a strip of material and for a group of people.
items.cn: 中古英语中用 band 指一条材料，也指一群人。

items.en: The musical sense grows from the idea of a company of players, and the radio sense from a strip of the frequency scale.
items.cn: 音乐义从「一队演奏者」发展而来，无线电义则来自频率刻度上的一条「带」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds built on band; the near-meaning group gathers strips, groups, and musical teams.
note.cn: 形近组收由 band 构成的复合词；近义组收带子、群体与音乐团队。

entries.definition: A strip of cloth used to cover a wound; it comes from the same strip word through French.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「绷带」，经法语来自同一个表示「带子」的词。

entries.definition: A band worn around the head.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「发带、头带」，由 head 与 band 组合而成。

entries.definition: The strip of cloth around the waist of a garment.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「腰头、腰带部分」，由 waist 与 band 组合而成。

entries.definition: The range of frequencies a signal uses, or the amount of data a connection can carry.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「带宽」，指信号占用的频率范围或连接的数据容量。

entries.definition: A long narrow piece of material; it matches the second sense without the binding idea.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「条、带」，对应第二个义项，但不含「捆扎」的意思。

entries.definition: A narrow decorative band of cloth, often tied in a bow.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「丝带、缎带」，多用于装饰，常打成蝴蝶结。

entries.definition: A number of people or things together; the general word for the fourth sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「群、组」，是第四个义项的一般说法。

entries.definition: A large group of musicians led by a conductor; larger and more formal than a band.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「管弦乐团」，规模比 band 更大、更正式。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real root meaning to bind, the compounds, and the everyday phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用词根「捆绑」的真实含义、复合词，以及这个词的日常搭配。

normal.en: The root means to bind, so a band is first the strip that ties things together.
normal.cn: 词根意为「捆绑」，所以 band 最初就是把东西捆在一起的带子。

normal.en: A rubber band stretches around a bundle and holds it, which shows the original image.
normal.cn: 橡皮筋绕着捆扎物一撑，就把它箍住，这正是最初的意象。

normal.en: A band of musicians is a group bound by playing together, not by a physical strip.
normal.cn: 乐队是因一起演奏而束在一起的一群人，并不是被实物带子捆住。

normal.en: Band together keeps the verb sense of tying people into one group.
normal.cn: band together 保留了把人「束」成一个群体的动词义。

normal.en: A radio band is a strip cut out of the whole range of frequencies.
normal.cn: 无线电波段就是从整个频率范围里切出来的一条。

abstract.en: Picture one cloth strip around a bundle of sticks: the sticks stay together because something goes around them.
abstract.cn: 想象一条布带绕住一捆木棍：木棍能聚在一起，是因为有东西绕在它们外面。

abstract.en: The same going-around appears in a wedding band, a headband, and a band of people standing together.
abstract.cn: 同样的「绕一圈」也出现在婚戒、发带和站在一起的一伙人身上。

abstract.en: English lets the strip become a range of waves, because both are long narrow pieces of a larger whole.
abstract.cn: 英语让这条带子变成一段波段，因为两者都是从更大整体里切出的狭长部分。

examples.en: The band played three songs at the school concert.
examples.cn: 乐队在学校音乐会上演奏了三首歌。

examples.cn: 他用橡皮筋把铅笔捆在一起。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of band all start from one strip that binds: the strip itself, the people bound into a group, the musicians bound by playing, a strip of radio frequencies, and the act of tying or uniting.
sensesIntro.cn: band 的五个义项都从一条起捆绑作用的带子出发：带子本身、被束成一伙的人、因演奏而聚的乐队、频率上的一个波段，以及捆绑或联合的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one cloth strip is wound around a bundle of sticks and pulled tight.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条布带绕住一捆木棍，被拉紧。

branches.en: THE STRIP: the oldest sense is the flat piece of material itself.
branches.cn: 带子线：最古老的义项就是那条扁平的实物。

branches.en: THE MUSIC: players bound together by a shared performance form a band.
branches.cn: 音乐线：因共同演出而聚在一起的演奏者构成乐队。

branches.en: THE WAVES: a narrow strip cut from the frequency scale is also a band.
branches.cn: 波段线：从频率刻度上切出的狭长一段也叫 band。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE: people tied by one purpose become a band, sometimes a band of thieves.
branches.cn: 人群线：被同一目的束在一起的人成为一伙，有时是盗贼一伙。

branches.en: THE ACT: the verb puts the strip around something or unites people into one body.
branches.cn: 动作线：动词把带子绕上去，或把人联合成一个整体。

definition_zh: 绷带；包扎；护带
definition_en: a strip of cloth used to cover and protect a wound
core_image: 一圈白布条绕在受伤的手指上
scene: 护士清洗完伤口，用一块干净的白布把手指包好。The nurse put a clean bandage on his cut finger.
sceneCN: 这里 bandage 是「绷带」（第 1 个义项：包扎伤口用的布条）；句意为护士给他割破的手指缠上了干净的绷带。

derivatives.zh: 由 bandage 加 -ed 构成，义为「包扎过的」
由 bandage 加 -ing 构成，义为「包扎、缠绷带」

senses.title: A strip for a wound
senses.definition: a strip of cloth or other material used to cover and protect a cut or injury
senses.definitionCN: 用来覆盖和保护伤口、割伤的布条或其他材料
senses.example: The nurse put a clean bandage on his cut finger.
senses.exampleCN: 护士给他割破的手指缠上了干净的绷带。
senses.why: The French word meant a strip, so the medical strip that wraps a wound is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 法语词本义是「带子」，所以缠住伤口的医用布条就是第一义。

senses.title: To wrap a wound
senses.definition: to cover or wrap a wound with a bandage
senses.definitionCN: 用绷带覆盖或缠住伤口
senses.example: She bandaged his knee after the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 他摔倒后，她给他的膝盖做了包扎。
senses.why: The verb turns the strip into an action: putting the strip around the injured part.
senses.whyCN: 动词把布条变成动作：把带子绕到受伤的部位上。

senses.title: A support for a joint
senses.definition: a firm strip worn around a joint to support or protect it
senses.definitionCN: 缠在关节上起支撑或保护作用的结实带子
senses.example: He wears a bandage on his wrist when he plays.
senses.exampleCN: 他打球时手腕上戴着护带。
senses.why: The same strip is used not only for cuts but for support, so protection of a joint is a further extension.
senses.whyCN: 同一条带子不仅用于伤口，也用于支撑，于是又扩展出保护关节的用法。

intro.en: Bandage comes from French and goes back to a Germanic word for a strip.
intro.cn: bandage 来自法语，可上溯到日耳曼语中表示「带子」的词。

items.en: The Germanic verb meaning to bind is the distant source of the strip word.
items.cn: 表示「捆绑」的日耳曼语动词是「带子」一词的远源。

items.en: Old French bande meant a strip or band of material.
items.cn: 古法语 bande 指一条材料或带子。

items.en: French formed bandage for a strip used in dressing a wound.
items.cn: 法语由 bande 构成 bandage，指包扎伤口用的布条。

items.en: English borrowed bandage as both a noun and a verb; the exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 英语把 bandage 同时借作名词和动词，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The medical sense became dominant, while the general strip sense faded.
items.cn: 医学义成为主要用法，泛指的「带子」义则逐渐消退。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the band family and the strip words; the near-meaning group gathers medical coverings and the act of wrapping.
note.cn: 形近组收 band 词族与表示带子的词；近义组收医用敷料与包扎动作。

entries.definition: A strip that ties or fastens; the direct source of bandage through French.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「带子」，是 bandage 经法语而来的直接来源。

entries.definition: Adjective meaning wrapped in a bandage.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「包扎过的」，由 bandage 加 -ed 构成。

entries.definition: A strip worn around the head; it shares the strip root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「发带」，与 bandage 共享「带子」词根。

entries.definition: A large printed handkerchief worn on the head; it only sounds similar and comes from Hindi.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「印花大头巾」；只是读音相近，词源来自印地语，与 bandage 无关。

entries.definition: A covering placed directly on a wound; broader than a bandage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「敷料」，直接覆在伤口上，范围比绷带更宽。

entries.definition: A small sticky strip placed over a cut; smaller than a bandage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「创可贴」，贴在伤口上的小粘条，比绷带小。

entries.definition: To cover something by folding material around it; the general verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「包裹」，是用材料把东西绕起来的一般说法。

entries.definition: A hard covering that holds a broken bone in place; heavier than a bandage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「石膏固定」，用于固定骨折，比绷带更硬更重。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real French origin, the strip image, and the medical phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的法语来源、「带子」意象，以及这个词的医用搭配。

normal.en: Bandage and band share the strip: a bandage is a strip made for a wound.
normal.cn: bandage 与 band 共享「带子」：绷带就是专为伤口做的带子。

normal.en: Put on a bandage is the everyday phrase for covering a cut.
normal.cn: put on a bandage 是处理割伤时最常用的说法。

normal.en: Bandage as a verb simply means to put the strip around the injury.
normal.cn: bandage 作动词，意思就是把带子绕到伤处。

normal.en: An elastic bandage stretches, so it can support a joint without stopping movement.
normal.cn: 弹性绷带可以拉伸，所以能支撑关节又不妨碍活动。

normal.en: Bandage up stresses wrapping the whole area, not just placing a small cover.
normal.cn: bandage up 强调把整片区域包起来，而不只是盖一小块。

abstract.en: Picture a white strip going around a finger three times: each turn is another layer of protection.
abstract.cn: 想象一条白布在手指上绕了三圈：每绕一圈就多一层保护。

abstract.en: The same strip becomes a verb, because a bandage is useless until someone wraps it.
abstract.cn: 同一条带子也能当动词用，因为不缠上去，绷带就没有用处。

abstract.en: A bandage does not heal the cut; it only holds the edges still so the body can heal itself.
abstract.cn: 绷带并不治愈伤口，它只是把边缘固定住，让身体自己愈合。

examples.en: The nurse put a clean bandage on his cut finger.
examples.cn: 护士给他割破的手指缠上了干净的绷带。

examples.en: She bandaged his knee after the fall.
examples.cn: 他摔倒后，她给他的膝盖做了包扎。

examples.en: He wears a bandage on his wrist when he plays.
examples.cn: 他打球时手腕上戴着护带。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「绑得紧」——白布条绑得紧紧，伤口就不乱动：绷带

root: bandage 经法语 bandage 来自古法语 bande「带子」，bande 又上溯到日耳曼语中表示「捆绑」的词根。本义是包扎用的布条，后兼作动词「包扎」，并扩展出支撑关节的「护带」义。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of bandage keep one strip in view: the strip for a wound, the act of wrapping it, and a support worn around a joint.
sensesIntro.cn: bandage 的三个义项都围绕同一条带子：包伤口的布条、把它缠上去的动作，以及缠在关节上的护带。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white strip circles an injured finger, layer over layer.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条白布绕着受伤的手指，一圈叠着一圈。

branches.en: THE STRIP: the word names the cloth itself before it names any action.
branches.cn: 布条线：这个词先指布本身，然后才指动作。

branches.en: THE ACT: wrapping the strip turns the noun into a verb.
branches.cn: 动作线：把布条缠上去，名词就变成了动词。

branches.en: THE JOINT: a firmer strip supports a wrist or knee without covering a cut.
branches.cn: 关节线：更结实的带子用来支撑手腕或膝盖，并不覆盖伤口。

branches.en: THE WOUND: the strip and the wrapping exist only because there is a cut to protect.
branches.cn: 伤口线：布条与缠绕之所以存在，只因为有伤口需要保护。

branches.en: THE PRESSURE: a firm wrap holds the edges still and gives the joint support.
branches.cn: 压力线：缠紧的布条固定边缘，也给关节支撑。

intro.en: Bandage is a French formation on the strip word, and English adds only ordinary inflections.
intro.cn: bandage 是在「带子」一词上形成的法语构词，英语只加上普通屈折成分。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic in origin and reached English through French; no Latin cognate is recorded, so the list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词源于日耳曼语，经法语进入英语，没有记录在案的拉丁同族词，因此列表留空。

definition_zh: 银行；岸；堤；一排；存钱；指望
definition_en: a business that keeps and lends money, or the land along the side of a river
core_image: 河岸的斜坡上长着草，水面在下面缓缓流过
scene: 河岸边长满高高的芦苇，孩子们坐在岸边钓鱼。They sat on the bank of the river and fished all afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里 bank 是「河岸」（第 2 个义项：河流旁边的陆地）；句意为他们坐在河岸上钓了一下午鱼。

derivatives.zh: 由 bank 加 -er 构成，义为「银行家」
由 bank 加 -ing 构成，义为「银行业务」
由 bank 与 note 组合而成，义为「纸币」
由 river 与 bank 组合而成，义为「河岸」

senses.title: A financial institution
senses.definition: a business that keeps money for people, lends money, and exchanges currency
senses.definitionCN: 替人保管钱、放贷并兑换货币的机构
senses.example: She went to the bank to open an account.
senses.exampleCN: 她去银行开了一个账户。
senses.why: Italian bankers worked at a bench or table, and the bench gave its name to the place that kept money.
senses.whyCN: 意大利的银行家在长凳或柜台前做生意，这条长凳的名字就成了保管钱财之地的名称。

senses.title: The land beside a river
senses.definition: the raised ground along the side of a river, lake, or canal
senses.definitionCN: 河流、湖泊或运河旁边隆起的土地
senses.example: They sat on the bank of the river and fished.
senses.exampleCN: 他们坐在河岸上钓鱼。
senses.why: The land sense comes from a different old word for a ridge or shelf, which describes the raised edge of a river.
senses.whyCN: 「岸」义来自另一个表示「隆起、台架」的古词，正好描述河边隆起的地形。

senses.title: A row or pile
senses.definition: a long row or a mass of things placed side by side, such as clouds or machines
senses.definitionCN: 并排摆放的一长排或一大堆东西，如云或机器
senses.example: A bank of clouds covered the western sky.
senses.exampleCN: 一堆云遮住了西边的天空。
senses.why: A raised ridge looks like a long heap, so any long heap or row takes the same name.
senses.whyCN: 隆起的埂看起来像长长的一堆，于是任何长排或长堆都叫这个名字。

senses.title: To keep money in a bank
senses.definition: to put money into a bank account
senses.definitionCN: 把钱存进银行账户
senses.example: He banks half of his pay every month.
senses.exampleCN: 他每月把一半工资存进银行。
senses.why: The verb turns the institution into an action: sending money to the place that keeps it.
senses.whyCN: 动词把机构变成动作：把钱送到保管它的地方。

senses.title: To depend on
senses.definition: in the phrase bank on, to depend on something happening
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 bank on，指指望某事发生
senses.example: You can bank on her to arrive on time.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以指望她准时到。
senses.why: Money placed in a bank is trusted to be safe, so to bank on something is to trust it like a deposit.
senses.whyCN: 存进银行的钱被认为安全可靠，所以 bank on 某事就像把钱存进去那样信任它。

intro.en: Bank has two histories that happen to meet in one spelling: the money word came through Italian and French, the land word from Norse.
intro.cn: bank 有两条恰好汇成一个拼写的历史：表示钱财的词经意大利语与法语而来，表示陆地的词来自诺尔斯语。

items.en: A Germanic word for a shelf or bench lies behind the money sense and is related to the ridge sense.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中表示「台架、长凳」的词是「银行」义的远源，与「隆起」义也有联系。

items.en: Italian banca meant a money-changer's bench or table, and from the table came the business.
items.cn: 意大利语 banca 指钱币兑换商的长凳或桌子，生意就从这张桌子得名。

items.en: French banque carried the financial word into English.
items.cn: 法语 banque 把这个财务词带入英语。

items.en: Old Norse bakki meant a ridge or the raised land beside a river, which gives the land sense.
items.cn: 古诺尔斯语 bakki 指隆起的埂或河边的陆地，这就是「岸」义的来源。

items.en: The two senses now live side by side, and bank on extends the money image to trust and reliance.
items.cn: 两个义项现在并存，bank on 又把「钱」的意象扩展到信任与依靠。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the bank family and compounds; the near-meaning group gathers financial places, shores, and rows.
note.cn: 形近组收 bank 词族与复合词；近义组收金融机构、岸边与成排之物。

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「银行家」，由 bank 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: The business of running banks.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「银行业务」，由 bank 加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: A piece of paper money issued by a bank.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「纸币」，由 bank 与 note 组合而成。

entries.definition: The land along the side of a river.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「河岸」，由 river 与 bank 组合而成。

entries.definition: The land along the edge of a sea or lake; wider than a river bank.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「海岸、湖岸」，范围比河岸更宽。

entries.definition: The land next to the sea, seen as a whole line.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「海岸」，指靠海的一整条陆地。

entries.definition: A line of things placed side by side; it matches the third sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一排」，对应第三个义项。

entries.definition: To put money into an account; the formal verb for the fourth sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「存入」，是第四个义项的正式说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Italian bench image, the Norse ridge image, and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的意大利语「长凳」意象、诺尔斯语「隆起」意象，以及这个词的常见搭配。

normal.en: Italian bankers worked at a bench called banca, so the bench became the bank.
normal.cn: 意大利银行家在叫作 banca 的长凳上做生意，长凳就成了「银行」。

normal.en: The river bank is a raised ridge of land, which is why a bank can also mean a heap.
normal.cn: 河岸是隆起的土埂，所以 bank 也能表示一堆东西。

normal.en: Bank account and bank money keep the financial sense in daily use.
normal.cn: bank account 与 bank money 让财务义留在日常使用中。

normal.en: A blood bank stores blood the way a money bank stores money.
normal.cn: 血库像银行存钱一样存放血液。

normal.en: Bank on someone means trusting that person like a safe deposit.
normal.cn: bank on 某人，就是像信任一笔安全存款那样信任他。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden bench in a market: coins are counted on it, and the bench slowly turns into an institution.
abstract.cn: 想象集市上一张木长凳：钱币在上面被清点，这张长凳慢慢变成了一所机构。

abstract.en: The same word also pictures a green slope above water, because both are raised edges people stand on.
abstract.cn: 同一个词还画出一条水上的绿色斜坡，因为两者都是人站立的隆起边缘。

abstract.en: Money and river never meet in the real world, yet English keeps them in one word because both are edges that hold something.
abstract.cn: 现实里钱与河并不相遇，英语却让它们共用一个词，因为两者都是「兜住东西的边缘」。

examples.en: They sat on the bank of the river and fished all afternoon.
examples.cn: 他们坐在河岸上钓了一下午鱼。

examples.en: She went to the bank to open an account.
examples.cn: 她去银行开了一个账户。

examples.en: You can bank on her to arrive on time.
examples.cn: 你可以指望她准时到。

root: 表示「银行」的 bank 经法语来自意大利语 banca「钱币兑换商的长凳」，可上溯到日耳曼语表示「台架、长凳」的词；表示「岸」的 bank 来自古诺尔斯语 bakki「隆起、河边陆地」。两条来源不同，现代同形。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of bank come from two old images that share one spelling: a bench where money is handled, and a raised edge of land, which also gives the row and the verb senses.
sensesIntro.cn: bank 的五个义项来自两个共用同一拼写的古老意象：处理钱币的长凳，以及隆起的土地边缘；后者又生出「一排」与动词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a low grassy slope rises above a river, while a wooden bench stands in a market.
core.cn: 核心意象：河面上方隆起一道长草的斜坡，集市上则摆着一张木长凳。

branches.en: THE BENCH: the money-changer's table becomes the institution that keeps money.
branches.cn: 长凳线：钱币兑换商的桌子变成了保管钱财的机构。

branches.en: THE RIDGE: the raised land beside a river is the second, separate origin.
branches.cn: 隆起线：河边隆起的土地是第二条独立来源。

branches.en: THE ROW: any long heap or line resembles that raised ridge.
branches.cn: 长排线：任何长堆或长排都像那道隆起的埂。

branches.en: THE DEPOSIT: the verb sends money to the bench that keeps it.
branches.cn: 存款线：动词把钱送到那张保管它的「长凳」上。

branches.en: THE TRUST: money kept safely becomes a model for relying on a person.
branches.cn: 信任线：被安全保管的钱，成了信任某个人的模型。

intro.en: Bank is a borrowed root with two histories; English expands it with -er, -ing and familiar compounds.
intro.cn: bank 是有两条来源的借入词根，英语用 -er、-ing 和常见复合词扩展它。

latinIntro.en: The financial sense passed through Italian banca, but that word is Germanic in origin, so no true Latin cognate is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 财务义经意大利语 banca 传来，但那个词本身源于日耳曼语，因此不列真正的拉丁同族词。

definition_zh: 棒球运动；棒球；棒球用的（作定语）
definition_en: a game in which two teams hit a ball with a bat and run around four bases
core_image: 一只白色小球被木棒击中，飞过内野
scene: 放学后，学生们戴上帽子，在操场上分组挥棒打球。Our class played baseball after school on Friday.
sceneCN: 这里 baseball 是「棒球运动」（第 1 个义项：用棒击球并跑垒的比赛）；句意为星期五放学后我们班打了棒球。

derivatives.zh: 由 baseball 与 cap 组合而成，义为「棒球帽」
由 baseball 与 bat 组合而成，义为「棒球棒」
由 baseball 与 player 组合而成，义为「棒球运动员」

senses.title: The sport
senses.definition: a game in which two teams take turns hitting a ball with a bat and running around four bases
senses.definitionCN: 两队轮流用棒击球、绕四个垒奔跑的比赛
senses.example: Our class played baseball after school on Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 星期五放学后我们班打了棒球。
senses.why: The compound joins base and ball, and the game is named after the two things a player uses most.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把 base 与 ball 合在一起，比赛正是按球员最常用的两样东西命名。

senses.title: The ball
senses.definition: the small hard ball used in this game, with a stitched cover
senses.definitionCN: 这项运动使用的、表面有缝线的小硬球
senses.example: He hit the baseball over the fence.
senses.exampleCN: 他把棒球击出了围栏。
senses.why: The second half of the compound keeps its literal meaning, so the object itself is also a baseball.
senses.whyCN: 复合词的后半保留了字面意思，所以那只球本身也叫 baseball。

senses.title: Of or for baseball
senses.definition: used before another noun to mean relating to or used in baseball
senses.definitionCN: 用在另一名词前，表示与棒球有关或供棒球使用
senses.example: He wore a blue baseball cap to the game.
senses.exampleCN: 他戴着一顶蓝色棒球帽去看比赛。
senses.why: Once the sport was well known, its name could stand in front of another noun as a label, like a badge.
senses.whyCN: 这项运动广为人知之后，它的名字就能放在另一名词前面作标签，像一枚徽章。

intro.en: Baseball is an English compound of base and ball, and the modern game took shape in the United States.
intro.cn: baseball 是 base 与 ball 的英语复合词，现代比赛形式在美国成形。

items.en: Greek basis meant a step or a pedestal, from the verb bainein, to go.
items.cn: 希腊语 basis 指台阶或基座，来自动词 bainein「走」。

items.en: Latin basis kept the sense of a base or foundation and passed through French into English as base.
items.cn: 拉丁语 basis 保留「基座、基础」之义，经法语以 base 进入英语。

items.en: Ball is the Germanic word for a round object, recorded in English from the Middle Ages.
items.cn: ball 是日耳曼语中表示圆形物的词，中古时期已见于英语。

items.en: The compound baseball is recorded in Britain in the eighteenth century, before the modern rules existed.
items.cn: baseball 这一复合词在十八世纪的英国已有记录，当时现代规则尚未形成。

items.en: The modern game with four bases and a bat spread in the United States in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 以四个垒和球棒为核心的现代比赛，在十九世纪的美国传播开来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the two halves of the compound and its common phrases; the near-meaning group gathers other bat-and-ball games and sports words.
note.cn: 形近组收这个复合词的两个成分及其常见搭配；近义组收其他用棒击球的运动和体育词。

entries.definition: One of the four points a player must reach in baseball, or the bottom part of something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「垒；底部」，是 baseball 的前半部分。

entries.definition: The round object hit in the game; the second half of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「球」，是 baseball 的后半部分。

entries.definition: The wooden or metal club used to hit the ball.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「棒球棒」，由 baseball 与 bat 组合而成。

entries.definition: A soft cap with a long front brim, worn in and out of the game.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「棒球帽」，帽檐较长，比赛内外都常戴。

entries.definition: A similar game played with a larger, softer ball.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「垒球」，规则相近，但用更大更软的球。

entries.definition: A bat-and-ball game popular in Britain and South Asia.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「板球」，是英国与南亚流行的击球运动。

entries.definition: An older British bat-and-ball game that resembles baseball.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「圆场球」，是英国较早的击球运动，与棒球相似。

entries.definition: The general word for a game played for exercise or competition.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「运动」，是这类活动的总称。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two real halves of the compound and the fixed phrases built on it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用这个复合词两个真实的组成部分，以及由它构成的固定搭配。

normal.en: Base plus ball: players run to bases and hit a ball, so the name lists the game's two essentials.
normal.cn: base 加 ball：球员跑垒、击球，名字正好列出比赛的两样核心。

normal.en: A baseball cap was first worn by players, then by everyone.
normal.cn: 棒球帽最初由球员佩戴，后来人人都戴。

normal.en: The ball in baseball is hard and small, unlike the bigger softball.
normal.cn: 棒球用的球又小又硬，与更大的垒球不同。

normal.en: A baseball field has four bases arranged in a diamond.
normal.cn: 棒球场有四个垒，排成菱形。

normal.en: Baseball came before basketball in English, and both names describe how the ball is used.
normal.cn: baseball 在英语中出现得比 basketball 早，两个名字都说明球的用法。

abstract.en: Picture a diamond of four white bags on the grass: a player must touch each one to score.
abstract.cn: 想象草地上四只白色垒包排成菱形：球员要逐个踩到才能得分。

abstract.en: The game is slow until the bat meets the ball, and then everyone moves at once.
abstract.cn: 比赛一直很慢，直到球棒击中球，所有人同时动起来。

abstract.en: One compound names a sport, a ball, and a hat, because a familiar word can label anything near it.
abstract.cn: 一个复合词可以指运动、球和帽子，因为熟悉的词能给身边任何东西贴标签。

examples.en: Our class played baseball after school on Friday.
examples.cn: 星期五放学后我们班打了棒球。

examples.en: He hit the baseball over the fence.
examples.cn: 他把棒球击出了围栏。

examples.en: She keeps her baseball cap in her school bag.
examples.cn: 她把棒球帽放在书包里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「贝斯包」——背个包去打球，包里装着球和棒：棒球

root: baseball 是英语复合词，由 base（经法语来自拉丁语 basis，源头为希腊语 basis「台阶、基座」）与 ball（日耳曼语「圆形物」）组合而成。十八世纪已有记录，现代四垒制比赛在十九世纪的美国成形。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of baseball start from one compound: the sport itself, the hard ball used in it, and the attributive use that labels caps, bats, and fields.
sensesIntro.cn: baseball 的三个义项都从一个复合词出发：运动本身、比赛用的硬球，以及给帽子、球棒、球场贴标签的定语用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white ball leaves the bat and rises over the infield grass.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只白球离开球棒，飞过内野草地。

branches.en: THE GAME: base and ball together name the sport of running the bases after a hit.
branches.cn: 比赛线：base 与 ball 合起来，指击球后跑垒的这项运动。

branches.en: THE BALL: the second half keeps its literal sense, so the hard stitched ball is also a baseball.
branches.cn: 球线：后半保留字面义，所以带缝线的硬球也叫 baseball。

branches.en: THE LABEL: the sport's name moves in front of caps, bats, and fields as a modifier.
branches.cn: 标签线：运动的名字移到帽子、球棒、球场前面作定语。

branches.en: THE EQUIPMENT: the bat, the glove, and the ball are all named through the game.
branches.cn: 装备线：球棒、手套和球都借这项运动来命名。

branches.en: THE FIELD: four bases in a diamond shape organize the whole game.
branches.cn: 球场线：四个垒排成菱形，组织起整场比赛。

intro.en: Baseball is a two-part English compound, and its parts are still visible and usable on their own.
intro.cn: baseball 是两部分组成的英语复合词，两个成分至今仍能独立使用。

latinIntro.en: The base half goes back to Latin basis from Greek, while ball is Germanic; basis is the recorded Latin form.
latinIntro.cn: 前半 base 可上溯到来自希腊语的拉丁语 basis，后半 ball 属日耳曼语；basis 是有记录的拉丁形式。

items.meaning: a bottom part, or one of four points in the game
items.exampleCN: 跑垒员到达了三垒。

items.example: The ball went over the fence.
items.exampleCN: 球飞过了围栏。

items.example: Baseball is popular in many countries.
items.exampleCN: 棒球在许多国家很受欢迎。

items.example: It forms baseballs, meaning the balls.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 baseballs，指多个棒球。

definition_zh: 基本的；基础的；简单的；基本知识；碱性的
definition_en: forming the base or most necessary part of something
core_image: 一座房子的地基埋在土里，上面的墙都靠它
scene: 上课前，老师先在黑板上写下三条最基本的规则。The teacher explained the basic rules before the game started.
sceneCN: 这里 basic 是「基本的」（第 1 个义项：构成基础、最必要的）；句意为比赛开始前老师讲解了基本规则。

pos.zh: 形容词：基本的；基础的；简单的；碱性的
名词：基本知识（常用复数）

derivatives.zh: 由 basic 加 -ally 构成，义为「基本上；大体上」
由 basic 加 -s 构成，义为「基本知识；基础」
基础词，义为「底部；基础」，basic 由它加后缀构成
与 base 同源的拉丁借词，义为「基础；根据」

senses.title: Fundamental
senses.definition: forming the base or the most necessary part of something
senses.definitionCN: 构成某物的基础或最必要部分
senses.example: The teacher explained the basic rules before the game.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛前老师讲解了基本规则。
senses.why: The word is built on base, so the first sense is whatever sits under everything else and holds it up.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在 base 之上，所以第一义就是垫在下面、支撑其余部分的东西。

senses.title: Simple, not advanced
senses.definition: simple and at an early level, without extra details
senses.definitionCN: 简单、处于初级水平，不带额外细节
senses.example: This book uses basic English for new readers.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书用简单的英语面向初学者。
senses.why: What is at the base comes before anything advanced, so basic also means the plain early level.
senses.whyCN: 处在底部的东西先于一切高级内容，所以 basic 也表示朴素的初级层次。

senses.title: Necessary for living
senses.definition: needed by everyone as a minimum for a decent life
senses.definitionCN: 人人过像样生活所需的最低条件
senses.example: Clean water is a basic need for every family.
senses.exampleCN: 干净的水是每个家庭的基本需求。
senses.why: If something is the base of life, it cannot be left out, which gives the sense of a minimum necessity.
senses.whyCN: 如果某物是生活的地基，就不能缺少，于是有了「最低必需」的义项。

senses.title: The essential facts
senses.definition: the simple, essential facts or skills of a subject, used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 某学科最简单、最必要的事实或技能，常用复数
senses.example: She taught me the basics of cooking.
senses.exampleCN: 她教了我烹饪的基本知识。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a noun for the things that form the base of a skill.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成名词，指构成某项技能之基础的那些内容。

senses.title: Alkaline
senses.definition: having the chemical properties of a base rather than an acid
senses.definitionCN: 具有碱而非酸的化学性质
senses.example: Soap is basic, so it can hurt your eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 肥皂是碱性的，所以可能刺激眼睛。
senses.why: Chemistry uses base for an alkaline substance, and the adjective basic follows that technical meaning.
senses.whyCN: 化学用 base 指碱，形容词 basic 就沿用了这个专业含义。

intro.en: Basic is an English adjective built on base, which goes back through French to Latin and Greek.
intro.cn: basic 是建立在 base 之上的英语形容词，base 经法语上溯到拉丁语与希腊语。

items.en: Greek basis meant a step or a pedestal, from bainein, to go.
items.cn: 希腊语 basis 指台阶或基座，来自 bainein「走」。

items.en: Latin basis kept the sense of a foundation and also gave the word for a chemical base.
items.cn: 拉丁语 basis 保留「基础」之义，也给出了化学中「碱」的名称。

items.en: English base arrives through Old French and means the bottom part that supports something.
items.cn: 英语 base 经古法语而来，指支撑某物的底部。

items.en: The adjective basic is formed by adding the Greek-derived suffix -ic to base.
items.cn: 形容词 basic 由 base 加上源自希腊语的后缀 -ic 构成。

items.en: The chemical sense is recorded in the nineteenth century, and the everyday sense of fundamental spreads in the twentieth.
items.cn: 化学义在十九世纪有记录，日常的「根本」义则在二十世纪广泛使用。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the base family; the near-meaning group gathers words for what is fundamental, simple, or essential.
note.cn: 形近组收 base 词族；近义组收表示根本、简单与必需的词。

entries.definition: The bottom part that supports something, or a main substance in chemistry.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「底部；基础；碱」，是 basic 的基础词。

entries.definition: In the main, in the simplest important respect.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「基本上、大体上」，由 basic 加 -ally 构成。

entries.definition: The simplest and most necessary facts or skills.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「基本知识、基础」，由 basic 加 -s 构成。

entries.definition: A round open container for water; it comes from a different Latin word and only looks similar.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「盆、水池」；只是拼写相近，词源来自另一个拉丁词，与 base 无关。

entries.definition: Forming the necessary centre of a system; stronger and more formal than basic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「根本的、基础的」，比 basic 更强调核心且更正式。

entries.definition: Absolutely necessary; it stresses need rather than level.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「必不可少的」，强调必要性而非层次。

entries.definition: At the simplest level of a subject; close to the second sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「初级的、基本的」，对应第二个义项。

entries.definition: Easy to understand or do, with nothing extra.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「简单的」，强调不复杂、无多余部分。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real base root, the suffix -ic, and the fixed phrases the adjective appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的 base 词根、后缀 -ic，以及这个形容词的固定搭配。

normal.en: Basic is base plus -ic, and a base is what everything else stands on.
normal.cn: basic 是 base 加 -ic，而 base 正是其他一切所站立之处。

normal.en: Basic English uses only simple words, which shows the second sense.
normal.cn: Basic English 只用简单词汇，体现第二个义项。

normal.en: Basic needs are food, water, and shelter, the minimum for life.
normal.cn: basic needs 是食物、水和住所，是生活的最低条件。

normal.en: The basics of a subject are what a beginner must learn first.
normal.cn: 一门学科的 basics 是初学者必须先学的内容。

normal.en: In chemistry a base is the opposite of an acid, so basic means alkaline.
normal.cn: 化学中 base 是酸的对立面，所以 basic 表示「碱性的」。

abstract.en: Picture a house: the walls and roof are visible, but only the buried foundation makes them possible.
abstract.cn: 想象一座房子：墙和屋顶看得见，但真正撑住它们的却是埋在地下的地基。

abstract.en: Remove the foundation and the house falls, just as a skill collapses without its basics.
abstract.cn: 抽掉地基房子就倒，正如技能失去基础就崩塌。

abstract.en: The same word covers a beginner's level and a chemical property, because both are starting points.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能指初学水平，也能指化学性质，因为两者都是「起点」。

examples.en: The teacher explained the basic rules before the game started.
examples.cn: 比赛开始前老师讲解了基本规则。

examples.en: This book uses basic English for new readers.
examples.cn: 这本书用简单的英语面向初学者。

examples.en: She taught me the basics of cooking.
examples.cn: 她教了我烹饪的基本知识。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「背此刻」——背下此刻的要点，才算打好基础：基本的

root: basic 由 base 加后缀 -ic 构成。base 经古法语来自拉丁语 basis，源头为希腊语 basis「台阶、基座」，来自动词 bainein「走」。故「基本的」义来自「垫在底下的基座」，化学中 base 又指「碱」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of basic all come from the image of a foundation: what supports everything, the simple early level, the minimum for life, the essential facts, and the chemical starting substance.
sensesIntro.cn: basic 的五个义项都来自「地基」意象：支撑一切的部分、朴素的初级层次、生活的最低条件、必备的基本知识，以及化学上的碱性物质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone foundation sits under a house, and every wall rests on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座房子的石基埋在下面，每一面墙都压在它上面。

branches.en: THE FOUNDATION: whatever holds the rest up is basic.
branches.cn: 地基线：凡是撑住其余部分的东西，就是 basic。

branches.en: THE LEVEL: what comes before advanced work is the simple early level.
branches.cn: 层次线：先于高级内容出现的，就是朴素的初级层次。

branches.en: THE MINIMUM: the base of a decent life cannot be left out.
branches.cn: 最低线：像样生活的地基不能缺少。

branches.en: THE FACTS: the essentials of a skill are its foundation in noun form.
branches.cn: 知识线：一项技能的要领，就是它名词形式的地基。

branches.en: THE CHEMISTRY: a base is the starting substance that neutralizes an acid.
branches.cn: 化学线：碱是能中和酸的起始物质。

intro.en: Basic is a Latin-derived base plus a Greek-derived adjective suffix, with ordinary English endings on top.
intro.cn: basic 是拉丁来源的 base 加希腊来源的形容词后缀，再叠加普通英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin basis is recorded and is the direct ancestor of base; the Greek form behind it is also recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 basis 有文献记录，是 base 的直接祖先；它背后的希腊语形式同样有记录。

items.example: The base of the statue is made of stone.
items.exampleCN: 雕像的底座是石头做的。
它由 base 构成 basic。

items.example: It forms basal, meaning at the base.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 basal，意为「基部的」。
它由 basic 构成 basically。

items.example: The basics are easy to learn.
items.exampleCN: 基本知识很容易学。

items.example: The report rests on a firm basis.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告建立在稳固的基础上。

items.example: The basal leaves lie flat on the ground.
items.exampleCN: 基部的叶子平贴在地面上。

items.example: The plan is basically the same.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划基本上是一样的。

latinEntries.meaning: the starting substance that neutralizes an acid
latinEntries.meaningCN: 碱；能与酸中和的起始物质

definition_zh: 篮子；筐；一篮之量；篮筐得分
definition_en: a container made of thin strips of material woven together, used to hold things
core_image: 一只竹编的篮子提在手里，里面装着水果
scene: 奶奶提着竹篮去市场，篮子里装满刚买的蔬菜。Grandma carried a basket to the market for vegetables.
sceneCN: 这里 basket 是「篮子」（第 1 个义项：编成的盛物容器）；句意为奶奶提着篮子去市场买蔬菜。

pos.zh: 名词：篮子；筐；一篮之量；篮筐得分

derivatives.zh: 由 basket 加 -ful 构成，义为「一满篮」
由 basket 加 -ry 构成，义为「编织工艺；篮子编织品」
由 basket 与 ball 组合而成，义为「篮球」

senses.title: A woven container
senses.definition: a container made of thin strips of cane, wire, or plastic woven together
senses.definitionCN: 用藤条、金属丝或塑料细条编成的容器
senses.example: Grandma carried a basket to the market for vegetables.
senses.exampleCN: 奶奶提着篮子去市场买蔬菜。
senses.why: The word first names the woven container itself, which is the object the old noun described.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最先指编成的容器本身，也就是那个古老名词所描述的东西。

senses.title: The amount one basket holds
senses.definition: the quantity of something that fills one basket
senses.definitionCN: 装满一只篮子的数量
senses.example: We picked a basket of apples in the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在园子里摘了一篮苹果。
senses.why: A container naturally measures its contents, so the object also becomes a unit of quantity.
senses.whyCN: 容器天然可以衡量所装之物，于是这件东西也成了计量单位。

senses.title: A score in basketball
senses.definition: the net and ring in basketball, or a goal scored by putting the ball through it
senses.definitionCN: 篮球的篮网与篮圈，或把球投进其中所得的分数
senses.example: He scored a basket in the last minute.
senses.exampleCN: 他在最后一分钟投中一球。
senses.why: The early basketball goal was literally a basket, so the hoop and the score kept the old container name.
senses.whyCN: 早期篮球的球篮真的就是一只篮子，所以篮筐与得分都沿用了这个容器名。

intro.en: Basket is recorded in Middle English, but its deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: basket 在中古英语中已有记录，但更早的来源不确定。

items.en: The word appears in Middle English as basket, naming a woven container.
items.cn: 这个词在中古英语中写作 basket，指编成的容器。

items.en: It is generally thought to come through Anglo-Norman French, though the source is not fully certain.
items.cn: 一般认为它经盎格鲁-诺曼法语传来，但来源并不完全确定。

items.en: The deeper origin is uncertain; some explanations point to a Celtic word, but this is not settled.
items.cn: 更早的来源不确定；有解释指向凯尔特语词，但并未定论。

items.en: English extended the word from the container to its contents and to the basketball hoop.
items.cn: 英语把这个词从容器扩展到所装的量，又扩展到篮球的篮筐。

items.en: Shopping basket and wastepaper basket show how the container sense keeps producing new compounds.
items.cn: shopping basket 与 wastepaper basket 说明容器义仍在不断构成新复合词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on basket; the near-meaning group gathers other containers and the basketball goal.
note.cn: 形近组收由 basket 构成的词；近义组收其他容器与篮球的篮筐。

entries.definition: The amount that fills one basket.

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real suffixes -ful and -ry, the compound basketball, and the fixed phrases with basket.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的后缀 -ful 与 -ry、复合词 basketball，以及 basket 的固定搭配。

normal.en: A basketful is exactly what one basket holds, so -ful turns the object into a quantity.
normal.cn: basketful 正是一只篮子所装的量，-ful 把器物变成数量。

normal.en: Basketry is the craft of making baskets, with -ry naming the skill.
normal.cn: basketry 是编篮子的手艺，-ry 表示这门技艺。

normal.en: Basketball was named after the basket that first served as the goal.
normal.cn: basketball 得名于最初当作球篮的那只篮子。

normal.en: A shopping basket holds what you pick before paying.
normal.cn: shopping basket 装着结账前挑选的东西。

normal.en: A wastepaper basket is a basket for paper you no longer need.
normal.cn: wastepaper basket 是装不再需要的废纸的篮子。

abstract.en: Picture woven strips crossing each other: no single strip is strong, but together they hold a heavy load.
abstract.cn: 想象细条彼此交错：单根不结实，合在一起却能承受重物。

abstract.en: An open basket holds things without hiding them, which is why it suits shopping and fruit.
abstract.cn: 敞口篮子装着东西却看得见，所以适合购物和装水果。

abstract.en: The same container became a goal in the air, and the word followed the object upward.
abstract.cn: 同一只容器被挂到空中当作球篮，这个词也跟着那件东西升了上去。

examples.en: He scored a basket in the last minute.

root: basket 记录于中古英语，一般认为经盎格鲁-诺曼法语传来，更早来源不确定，有解释指向凯尔特语词但未定论。词义由编织容器扩展到「一篮之量」，又因早期篮球以篮子为球篮而扩展出「篮筐、投中」义。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of basket move from the woven container to its measured contents, and then to the hoop that borrowed the container's name.
sensesIntro.cn: basket 的三个义项从编织容器，到它量出的内容，再到借用了容器之名的篮筐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: thin woven strips cross and hold a heap of fruit.
core.cn: 核心意象：细条交错编成容器，托住一堆水果。

branches.en: THE CONTAINER: the first sense is the woven vessel itself.
branches.cn: 容器线：第一义就是那只编成的盛器。

branches.en: THE CONTENTS: a basket naturally measures what it carries.
branches.cn: 内容线：篮子天然衡量它所装的东西。

branches.en: THE HOOP: the early basketball goal was a real basket, and the name stayed.
branches.cn: 篮筐线：早期篮球的球篮真是篮子，名字就留了下来。

branches.en: THE MARKET: baskets carry fruit and vegetables, so shopping keeps the word alive.
branches.cn: 集市线：篮子装水果蔬菜，购物场景让这个词一直活跃。

branches.en: THE SCORE: putting the ball through the hoop is counted as a basket.
branches.cn: 得分线：把球投进篮筐，就算得到一个 basket。

intro.en: Basket is an old borrowed noun; English expands it with -ful, -ry, and compounds.
intro.cn: basket 是古老的借入名词，英语用 -ful、-ry 和复合构词来扩展它。

definition_en: a game in which two teams try to throw a ball through a high hoop

sceneCN: 这里 basketball 是「篮球运动」（第 1 个义项：把球投进高篮的比赛）；句意为每周三我们都在体育馆打篮球。
