senses.title: The sport
senses.definition: a game in which two teams try to throw a ball through a high hoop to score points
senses.definitionCN: 两队设法把球投进高处的篮圈来得分
senses.example: We play basketball in the gym every Wednesday.
senses.exampleCN: 每周三我们都在体育馆打篮球。
senses.why: The name joins basket and ball, and the game is named after the goal and the object used to reach it.

senses.title: The ball
senses.definition: the large round ball used in this game, usually orange with a rough surface
senses.definitionCN: 这项运动使用的大圆球，通常为橙色、表面粗糙

intro.en: Basketball is a late nineteenth-century American compound, coined together with the game itself.
intro.cn: basketball 是十九世纪后期美国的复合词，与这项运动同时被创造出来。

items.en: Basket is the old woven-container word, of uncertain deeper origin.
items.cn: basket 是古老的「编织容器」词，更早来源不确定。

items.en: Ball is the Germanic word for a round object used in games.
items.cn: ball 是日耳曼语中表示游戏用圆球的词。

items.en: The game was invented in Springfield, Massachusetts, and the name was formed from the peach baskets used as goals.
items.cn: 这项运动于一八九一年在马萨诸塞州斯普林菲尔德被发明，名字来自当时用作球篮的桃筐。

items.en: The first goals were real baskets, and the ball had to be taken out by hand after each score.
items.cn: 最初的球篮真是篮子，每次得分后还要用手把球取出来。

items.en: The word now names the sport, the ball, and the places and people connected with it.
items.cn: 这个词现在指运动、球，以及与之相关的场地和人。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds built on basketball; the near-meaning group gathers other ball games and related equipment.
note.cn: 形近组收由 basketball 构成的复合词；近义组收其他球类运动与相关装备。

entries.definition: The woven container that first served as the goal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「篮子」，最初被当作球篮使用，是 basketball 的前半部分。

entries.definition: The marked area where the game is played.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「篮球场」，指划好线的比赛场地。

entries.definition: The ring and net through which the ball must pass.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「篮圈、篮网」，球必须穿过它。

entries.definition: Another ball game whose name joins an action word and ball.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「排球」，构词方式相同，也是行为词加 ball。

entries.definition: A similar team game in which players throw a ball into a net.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「无板篮球」，规则相近，把球投进网中。

entries.definition: A game in which players throw a ball into a goal with their hands.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「手球」，用手把球投进球门。

entries.definition: The ring used as the goal in basketball.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「篮圈」，是篮球的得分目标。

entries.definition: The marked playing area for games such as basketball and tennis.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「球场」，指篮球、网球等划线的比赛场地。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real origin of the name, its two halves, and the fixed phrases built on it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用这个名字的真实来源、两个组成部分，以及由它构成的固定搭配。

normal.en: Basket plus ball: the first goal was a real basket, and the ball had to go into it.
normal.cn: basket 加 ball：最初的球篮真是篮子，球必须投进去。

normal.en: A basketball court is the floor, and a basketball hoop is the ring above it.
normal.cn: basketball court 是地面，basketball hoop 是上方的篮圈。

normal.en: The ball is orange and rough so that players can grip and bounce it.
normal.cn: 篮球是橙色且表面粗糙，便于抓握和拍打。

normal.en: Play basketball uses no article, just like play football and play chess.
normal.cn: play basketball 不加冠词，就像 play football 和 play chess。

normal.en: Basketball and volleyball share the same naming pattern: an action or object plus ball.
normal.cn: basketball 与 volleyball 构词相同：一个动作或物件加 ball。

abstract.en: Picture a peach basket nailed high on a wall: someone throws a ball up, and the game begins.
abstract.cn: 想象一只桃筐被钉在高墙上：有人把球往上抛，比赛就开始了。

abstract.en: The hoop is small and the ball is large, so every score needs aim rather than force.
abstract.cn: 篮圈小而球大，所以每次得分靠的是准头而不是蛮力。

abstract.en: A game invented for a winter gym kept the name of the fruit basket it started with.
abstract.cn: 一项为冬季体育馆发明的运动，保留了它最初那只水果筐的名字。

examples.en: We play basketball in the gym every Wednesday.
examples.cn: 每周三我们都在体育馆打篮球。

examples.en: He bounced the basketball twice before shooting.
examples.cn: 他拍了两下篮球才投篮。

examples.en: Our basketball team won the school match.
examples.cn: 我们的篮球队赢了校际比赛。

root: basketball 是十九世纪末的美国英语复合词，由 basket（古老的「编织容器」词，更早来源不确定）与 ball（日耳曼语「圆球」）组合而成。因最初以桃筐作球篮而得名，现指运动、球及相关的场地与人员。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses of basketball come from one compound: the sport named after its basket goal, and the orange ball thrown through it.
sensesIntro.cn: basketball 的两个义项来自同一个复合词：以球篮命名的运动，以及投进篮圈的那只橙色球。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an orange ball drops through a high net and pulls the cords tight.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只橙色球穿过高处的篮网，把网绳拉紧。

branches.en: THE SPORT: basket and ball together name the game of throwing at a high goal.
branches.cn: 运动线：basket 与 ball 合起来，指朝高处目标投球的比赛。

branches.en: THE BALL: the second half keeps its literal sense, so the orange ball is a basketball.
branches.cn: 球线：后半保留字面义，所以那只橙色球就叫 basketball。

branches.en: THE HOOP: the basket that gave the game its name still hangs above the court.
branches.cn: 篮圈线：为比赛命名的「篮子」至今仍挂在球场上空。

branches.en: THE TEAM: five players pass and shoot together, so the sport is played by sides.
branches.cn: 球队线：五名球员一起传球投篮，所以这项运动按队进行。

branches.en: THE SURFACE: the rough orange cover exists so the ball can be gripped and bounced.
branches.cn: 表面线：粗糙的橙色外皮是为了便于抓握与拍打。

intro.en: Basketball is a modern two-part compound whose halves are still common words.
intro.cn: basketball 是近代的两部分复合词，两个成分至今都是常用词。

latinIntro.en: Neither half is Latin: basket is a borrowing of uncertain origin, and ball is Germanic, so the list is empty.

definition_zh: 蝙蝠；球棒；球拍；用棒击球
definition_en: a small animal that flies at night, or a wooden club used to hit a ball
core_image: 夜里一只蝙蝠擦着屋檐飞过，翅膀薄得像纸
scene: 傍晚的屋檐下，一只黑色的小动物贴着墙飞快掠过，几乎看不清。A bat flew out of the old cave at dusk.
sceneCN: 这里 bat 是「蝙蝠」（第 1 个义项：会飞的哺乳动物）；句意为黄昏时一只蝙蝠从旧山洞里飞了出来。

senses.title: The flying animal
senses.definition: a small furry animal with wings that flies at night and rests upside down by day
senses.definitionCN: 白天倒挂休息、夜间飞行的小型毛茸茸动物，长有翼膜
senses.example: A bat flew out of the old cave at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 黄昏时一只蝙蝠从旧山洞里飞了出来。
senses.why: The animal sense comes from an old word for this creature, which is unrelated to any club.
senses.whyCN: 动物义来自指这种动物的古词，与任何「棍棒」都没有关系。

senses.title: A club for hitting a ball
senses.definition: a specially shaped wooden or metal club used to hit a ball in games
senses.definitionCN: 比赛中用来击球的、形状特制的木制或金属棒
senses.example: He picked up the bat and walked to the plate.
senses.exampleCN: 他拿起球棒，走向击球位置。
senses.why: The club sense comes from a separate old word meaning a stick or a blow, and only the spelling is shared with the animal.
senses.whyCN: 「球棒」义来自另一个表示「棍子、击打」的古词，与动物义只是共用拼写而已。

senses.title: To hit with a bat
senses.definition: to hit a ball with a bat, or to take a turn at hitting
senses.definitionCN: 用球棒击球，或轮到上场击球
senses.example: She batted the ball far into the outfield.
senses.exampleCN: 她把球击到很远的外野。
senses.why: The verb is the club in action: swinging the stick so that it strikes the ball.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是那条球棒在动作：挥动棍子让它击中球。

intro.en: Bat is two different words with one spelling: the animal and the club each have their own history.
intro.cn: bat 是两个共用一个拼写的不同词：动物义与棍棒义各有自己的历史。

items.en: The animal word appears in Middle English in forms like bakke, and its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 动物义在中古英语中以 bakke 等形式出现，更早来源不确定。

items.en: Related forms for the animal occur in Scandinavian languages, which supports a northern source, though this is not settled.
items.cn: 斯堪的纳维亚诸语中有指这种动物的相关形式，支持北方来源，但尚未定论。

items.en: A separate word batt meant a stick or a blow, and it is the source of the club sense.
items.cn: 另有一个古英语词 bat，意为「棍子、击打」，是「球棒」义的来源。

items.en: The club word spread with bat-and-ball games, and the verb to bat followed the noun.
items.cn: 棍棒词随击球运动传播，动词 bat 则由名词而来。

items.en: The two words now look identical, and only the context tells you whether the animal or the club is meant.
items.cn: 两个词现在完全同形，只能靠上下文判断指的是动物还是球棒。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the club sense; the near-meaning group gathers the animal, the club, and the act of hitting.
note.cn: 形近组收由「棍棒」义构成的词；近义组收这种动物、球棒以及击球动作。

entries.definition: The player who hits with the bat, or a mixture beaten together in cooking.

entries.definition: The act or turn of hitting the ball with a bat.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「击球」，由 bat 加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: Informal adjective meaning slightly crazy, as if fluttering like a bat.
entries.definitionCN: 口语形容词，义为「古怪的、有点疯的」，像蝙蝠一样乱飞。

entries.definition: A thin stick used by a conductor or a runner; it comes from French and only looks similar.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「指挥棒、接力棒」；只是拼写相近，词源来自法语，与 bat 无关。

entries.definition: A heavy stick used to hit; broader and rougher than a bat.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「棍棒」，比球棒更粗更泛。

entries.definition: A bat with strings, used in tennis and badminton.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「球拍」，带网线，用于网球与羽毛球。

entries.definition: A night bird; like a bat it is active after dark, but it is a bird.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「猫头鹰」，也夜间活动，但属鸟类。

entries.definition: To move a bat or club through the air in order to hit.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「挥动」，指把球棒或棍棒挥向球。

normal.cn: bat the ball 显示动词用法：棍子一挥，球就飞走。

root: bat 有两条互不相关的来源：表示「蝙蝠」的词见于中古英语 bakke 等形式，更早来源不确定，斯堪的纳维亚诸语中有相关形式；表示「棍棒、击打」的 bat 来自古英语 bat，是「球棒」与动词「击球」的来源。两者现代同形。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of bat come from two separate words that share a spelling: the flying animal, the club, and the act of swinging that club.
sensesIntro.cn: bat 的三个义项来自两个共用同一拼写的不同词：会飞的动物、击球的棍棒，以及挥动那根棍棒的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin wing cuts through the evening air while a smooth wooden club waits on the ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片薄翼划过傍晚的空气，地上则静静靠着一根光滑的木棒。

branches.en: THE ANIMAL: one old word names the creature that flies after dark.
branches.cn: 动物线：一个古词指这种天黑后飞行的生物。

branches.en: THE CLUB: a different old word names the stick used to strike a ball.
branches.cn: 棍棒线：另一个古词指用来击球的棍子。

branches.en: THE ACT: the verb is the club swinging into the ball.
branches.cn: 动作线：动词就是球棒挥向球。

branches.en: THE NIGHT: the animal is tied to dusk, caves, and eaves.
branches.cn: 夜晚线：这种动物与黄昏、山洞、屋檐连在一起。

branches.en: THE GAME: the club and the swing exist for bat-and-ball sports.
branches.cn: 比赛线：球棒与挥击都是为击球运动而存在。

intro.en: Bat is a short root with two histories; English adds -er, -ing and -y to build its small family.
intro.cn: bat 是有两条历史的短词根，英语用 -er、-ing、-y 构成它的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Neither sense is Latin in origin and no Latin cognate is recorded, so the list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 两个义项都不源于拉丁语，也没有记录在案的拉丁同族词，因此列表留空。

definition_zh: 浴室；卫生间；洗手间
definition_en: a room with a bath or shower, or a room with a toilet
core_image: 一间小房里，浴缸和镜子并排摆在墙边
scene: 旅馆房间很小，门后这间屋子只有一个洗脸池和一面镜子。Excuse me, where is the bathroom?
sceneCN: 这里 bathroom 是「洗手间」（第 2 个义项：委婉说法，指有马桶的房间）；句意为「打扰一下，洗手间在哪里？」。

pos.zh: 名词：浴室；卫生间；洗手间

derivatives.zh: 基础词，义为「洗澡、浴缸」，是 bathroom 的前半部分
由 bathroom 与 fittings 组合而成，义为「卫浴配件」
由 bathroom 与 mirror 组合而成，义为「浴室镜」

senses.title: A room for washing
senses.definition: a room containing a bath or shower, used for washing the body
senses.definitionCN: 装有浴缸或淋浴、用来清洗身体的房间
senses.example: He steamed up the bathroom mirror with a hot shower.
senses.exampleCN: 热水淋浴使浴室镜子蒙上了雾气。
senses.why: The compound joins bath and room, so its first sense is literally the room built for bathing.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把 bath 与 room 合在一起，第一义就是为洗澡而造的房间。

senses.title: A room with a toilet
senses.definition: a room containing a toilet, used especially as a polite word in American English
senses.definitionCN: 装有马桶的房间，在美式英语中尤用作委婉说法
senses.example: Excuse me, where is the bathroom?
senses.exampleCN: 打扰一下，洗手间在哪里？
senses.why: Polite usage shifted the word from the bath to the toilet, since naming the function directly feels blunt.
senses.whyCN: 出于礼貌，这个词从「浴缸」转到了「马桶」，因为直接说那个功能显得太直白。

senses.title: The fixtures as a set
senses.definition: the fittings of such a room, such as the sink, tub, and tiles, when sold as a set
senses.definitionCN: 这类房间的成套配件，如水池、浴缸与瓷砖，常成套出售
senses.example: The shop sells bathroom fittings in matching colours.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店出售颜色相配的卫浴配件。
senses.why: Because the word names the room, it can also label the whole set of objects that belong in that room.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词指一间房，也能给属于这间房的整套物件贴标签。

intro.en: Bathroom is a plain English compound of bath and room, and the polite toilet sense developed later in America.
intro.cn: bathroom 是 bath 与 room 构成的朴素英语复合词，委婉的「洗手间」义后在美国发展出来。

items.en: Old English bæþ meant a bath or the act of bathing, from a Germanic root.
items.cn: 古英语 bæþ 指浴缸或洗澡这件事，来自日耳曼语词根。

items.en: Related words for bathing appear across the Germanic languages, which confirms the root.
items.cn: 日耳曼诸语中都有表示洗澡的相关词，印证了这一词根。

items.en: Room first meant space, then a separate space inside a building.
items.cn: room 最初指空间，后来指建筑内部的一块独立空间。

items.en: Bathroom is recorded in the eighteenth century as the room used for bathing.
items.cn: bathroom 在十八世纪已有记录，指用于洗澡的房间。

items.en: American English extended the word to any room with a toilet, as a polite substitute.
items.cn: 美式英语把这个词扩展到任何带马桶的房间，作为委婉说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the two halves of the compound and its relatives; the near-meaning group gathers other words for washing and toilet rooms.
note.cn: 形近组收这个复合词的两个成分及其亲属词；近义组收其他表示浴室与洗手间的词。

entries.definition: A tub for washing the body, or the act of washing in it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「浴缸；洗澡」，是 bathroom 的前半部分。

entries.definition: A room for sleeping, built the same way as bathroom.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「卧室」，构词方式与 bathroom 相同。

entries.definition: A room with washing facilities, often a polite word for a toilet in Canada.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「洗手间」，构词方式相同，在加拿大常作委婉说法。

entries.definition: A loose robe worn before or after bathing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「浴袍」，洗澡前后穿的宽松长袍。

entries.definition: The fixture itself, or the room containing it; more direct than bathroom.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「马桶；卫生间」，比 bathroom 更直接。

entries.definition: A public toilet room; the usual American word for one in a building.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「公共洗手间」，美式英语中常用于建筑内的设施。

entries.definition: A device that sprays water for washing, or the act of washing under it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「淋浴；淋浴器」，常在浴室中使用。

entries.definition: A toilet, or the room containing one; formal in British English.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「盥洗室、厕所」，英式英语中较正式。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two real halves of the compound, the parallel words like bedroom, and the phrases it appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用这个复合词两个真实的组成部分、bedroom 这类平行词，以及它的常见搭配。

normal.en: Bath plus room is as literal as bedroom: one room for bathing, one room for sleeping.
normal.cn: bath 加 room 和 bedroom 一样直白：一间洗澡，一间睡觉。

normal.en: In America, go to the bathroom is the polite way to say you need the toilet.
normal.cn: 在美国，go to the bathroom 是说要上厕所的委婉说法。

normal.en: Bathroom mirror and bathroom door show the room sense in daily use.
normal.cn: bathroom mirror 与 bathroom door 体现「房间」义的日常用法。

normal.en: A shared bathroom means more than one person uses the same room.
normal.cn: shared bathroom 意为不止一个人共用这间房。

normal.en: Bathroom fittings are the objects installed in that room, sold as a group.
normal.cn: bathroom fittings 是装在这间房里的物件，常成套出售。

abstract.en: Picture a small tiled room with a tub on one side and a mirror on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一间铺着瓷砖的小屋，一边是浴缸，一边是镜子。

abstract.en: The same room can be described by what you wash in or by what you cannot name directly, which is why the polite sense grew.
abstract.cn: 同一间房既可按洗澡的器具来称呼，也可因不便直说而换个说法，这就是委婉义产生的原因。

abstract.en: English builds many room words by joining a purpose and the word room, like bedroom and classroom.
abstract.cn: 英语用「用途加 room」造了许多房间词，如 bedroom 与 classroom。

examples.en: He steamed up the bathroom mirror with a hot shower.
examples.cn: 热水淋浴使浴室镜子蒙上了雾气。

examples.en: Excuse me, where is the bathroom?
examples.cn: 打扰一下，洗手间在哪里？

examples.en: The flat has a small bathroom and two bedrooms.
examples.cn: 这套公寓有一个小浴室和两个卧室。

root: bathroom 是 bath 与 room 的英语复合词。bath 来自古英语 bæþ「洗澡、浴缸」，源于日耳曼语；room 由「空间」引申为「房间」。十八世纪已有记录，美式英语后来把它扩展为带马桶房间的委婉说法。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of bathroom start from the literal room for bathing, move to the polite word for a toilet room, and end with the set of fittings sold for that room.
sensesIntro.cn: bathroom 的三个义项从字面上的洗澡房间，转到指马桶房间的委婉说法，最后落到为这间房成套出售的配件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tiled room with a tub, a sink, and a mirror on the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间铺瓷砖的小屋，装着浴缸、水池和墙上的镜子。

branches.en: THE ROOM: bath and room together name the place built for washing.
branches.cn: 房间线：bath 与 room 合起来，指为洗澡而建的地方。

branches.en: THE TOILET: politeness moves the name from the tub to the fixture people avoid naming.
branches.cn: 马桶线：出于礼貌，名字从浴缸移到人们不愿直呼的器具。

branches.en: THE FITTINGS: the room's name labels the whole set of objects inside it.
branches.cn: 配件线：房间的名字给里面整套物件贴了标签。

branches.en: THE MIRROR: washing and shaving happen before the mirror, a daily scene in this room.
branches.cn: 镜子线：洗漱与刮脸都在镜前进行，是这间房的日常场景。

branches.en: THE BREAK: a bathroom break is the polite way to ask for time away.
branches.cn: 休息线：bathroom break 是想离开一会儿时的委婉说法。

intro.en: Bathroom is one of the many English room compounds; both halves are still ordinary words.
intro.cn: bathroom 是英语众多「房间」复合词之一，两个成分至今都是普通词。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are Germanic, so no Latin cognate is recorded and the list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 两个成分都属日耳曼语，没有记录在案的拉丁同族词，因此列表留空。

definition_zh: 是；存在；成为；处于；发生（用于构成时态与被动）
definition_en: to exist, to have a quality, or to be in a state or place
core_image: 一面镜子里映出的就是眼前这个东西本身
scene: 毕业册上，男孩写下将来的愿望，说想当一名医生。He wants to be a doctor when he grows up.
sceneCN: 这里 be 是「成为」（第 4 个义项：将来取得某种身份）；句意为他长大后想当一名医生。

pos.zh: 助动词：构成进行时与被动语态

forms.label: 第一与第三人称单数过去式

derivatives.zh: 由 be 加 -ing 构成，义为「存在；生物」
由 may 与 be 组合而成，义为「也许」
由 well 与 being 组合而成，义为「幸福安康」

senses.title: To have a quality or identity
senses.definition: used to link a subject with a noun or adjective that describes it
senses.definitionCN: 用来把主语与描述它的名词或形容词连起来
senses.example: She is a student and her brother is a teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 她是学生，她哥哥是老师。
senses.why: The oldest use simply puts two things side by side as the same, so linking subject and description is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的用法只是把两样东西并排视为同一，所以把主语与描述连起来就是第一义。

senses.title: To exist
senses.definition: to exist or to be present in a place
senses.definitionCN: 存在，或位于某个地方
senses.example: There are three chairs in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里有三把椅子。
senses.why: Before anything can be described, it must simply be there, so existence is the second sense.
senses.whyCN: 任何东西在被描述之前，必须先「在那里」，所以「存在」是第二义。

senses.title: To be in a state
senses.definition: used with an adjective or phrase to describe a temporary state or condition
senses.definitionCN: 与形容词或短语连用，描述暂时的状态或情况
senses.example: He is tired after the long walk.
senses.exampleCN: 走了很久之后他很累。
senses.why: Identity and existence combine into a state: the thing is here, and here is how it is.
senses.whyCN: 「是什么」与「在那里」合成状态：东西在这里，而且它是这个样子。

senses.title: To become
senses.definition: used in phrases such as be a doctor to mean to become one
senses.definitionCN: 用于 be a doctor 这类说法，表示成为某种身份
senses.example: She wants to be a doctor when she grows up.
senses.exampleCN: 她长大后想当医生。
senses.why: A future identity is spoken of as if it already holds, so being something can also mean becoming it.
senses.whyCN: 未来的身份被说得好像已经成立，所以「是某种人」也能表示「成为某种人」。

senses.title: Auxiliary for tenses and passive
senses.titleCN: 助动词：构成时态与被动
senses.definition: used with a participle to form the continuous tenses or the passive voice
senses.definitionCN: 与分词连用，构成进行时或被动语态
senses.example: The bridge was built last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥是去年建成的。
senses.why: Once be can state a condition, it can also hold another verb's action in that condition, which gives the auxiliary use.
senses.whyCN: 既然 be 能陈述状态，它也能把另一个动词的动作放进这个状态里，于是有了助动词用法。

intro.en: Be is the most irregular verb in English because it merged forms from three different old roots.
intro.cn: be 是英语中最不规则的动词，因为它把三个不同古老词根的形式合并在一起。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning to grow or to become lies behind the am, is, are forms.
items.cn: 一个可重构、意为「生长、成为」的词根，是 am、is、are 这些形式的远源。

items.en: Old English had beon, to be or to become, and also wesan, to remain or exist.
items.cn: 古英语既有 beon「是、成为」，也有 wesan「存在、停留」。

items.en: The forms am and is come from a different root that meant to exist.
items.cn: am 与 is 来自另一个表示「存在」的词根。

items.en: Middle English joined these sets into one verb, which is why its forms look so unlike each other.
items.cn: 中古英语把这些形式合并成一个动词，所以它的各形式看起来彼此很不相同。

items.en: The auxiliary uses for continuous and passive sentences became standard in later English.
items.cn: 构成进行时与被动句的助动词用法，在后来的英语中成为标准。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the forms of the same verb; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs that express existence or a state.
note.cn: 形近组收同一个动词的各种形式；近义组收表示存在或状态的其他动词。

entries.definition: The third person singular present form of be.
entries.definitionCN: be 的第三人称单数现在时形式。

entries.definition: The present plural form of be, also used with you.
entries.definitionCN: be 的现在时复数形式，也用于第二人称。

entries.definition: The past form of be for I, he, she and it.
entries.definitionCN: be 用于第一、第三人称单数的过去式。

entries.definition: The past participle of be, used after have.
entries.definitionCN: be 的过去分词，用在 have 之后。

entries.definition: To be real or present; a more formal verb for the second sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「存在」，是第二个义项的正式说法。

entries.definition: To begin to be something; it makes the fourth sense explicit.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「成为」，把第四个义项说明得更清楚。

entries.definition: To continue to be in a state; it stresses staying rather than starting.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「仍然是」，强调持续而非开始。

entries.definition: To appear to be something, without saying that it truly is.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「似乎」，表示看起来是，而不断言确实是。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real history of the merged forms and the everyday phrases built with be.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用这些形式合并的真实历史，以及由 be 构成的日常搭配。

normal.en: Am, is and are come from one old root, while was and were come from another, which is why the verb looks irregular.
normal.cn: am、is、are 来自一个古老词根，was、were 来自另一个，所以这个动词看起来不规则。

normal.en: Been is the past participle, so it appears after have: I have been there.
normal.cn: been 是过去分词，所以出现在 have 之后：I have been there。

normal.en: Being is both the present participle and a noun meaning a living creature.
normal.cn: being 既是现在分词，也是名词，指活着的生物。

normal.en: Be careful and be sure use be plus an adjective to describe a state.
normal.cn: be careful 与 be sure 用 be 加形容词来描述状态。

normal.en: Be from asks about origin, while be at asks about place.
normal.cn: be from 问来源，be at 问地点。

abstract.en: Picture a mirror: it adds nothing to what stands before it, it only says that the thing is.
abstract.cn: 想象一面镜子：它不给眼前的东西增添什么，只是确认那东西「在」。

abstract.en: The same small word holds identity, place, state, and time, because all four answer the question of what is.
abstract.cn: 同一个小词装着身份、位置、状态与时间，因为四者都在回答「什么在」。

abstract.en: English kept the most-used verb the most irregular, because everyone says it too often to change it.
abstract.cn: 英语把最常用的动词保留得最不规则，因为人人说得太多，反而改不动它。

examples.en: She is a student and her brother is a teacher.
examples.cn: 她是学生，她哥哥是老师。

examples.en: There are three chairs in the room.
examples.cn: 房间里有三把椅子。

examples.en: The bridge was built last year.
examples.cn: 这座桥是去年建成的。

root: be 由三个古老词源合并而成：beon「是、成为」、wesan「存在、停留」，以及给出 am、is 的另一个「存在」词根；可上溯到原始印欧语重构形式。中古英语把这些形式并成一个动词，因此变位极不规则。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of be all answer what is: what something is, that it exists, how it is, what it will become, and what is done to it.
sensesIntro.cn: be 的五个义项都在回答「什么在」：某物是什么、它存在、它处于什么状态、它将变成什么，以及它被做了什么。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mirror shows the object in front of it exactly as it is.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面镜子把眼前的东西原样映出来。

branches.en: THE IDENTITY: the verb links a subject with what it is.
branches.cn: 身份线：这个动词把主语与它是什么连起来。

branches.en: THE EXISTENCE: before description, the thing must simply be there.
branches.cn: 存在线：在被描述之前，东西必须先在那里。

branches.en: THE STATE: identity plus place gives a temporary condition.
branches.cn: 状态线：身份加位置合成暂时的状况。

branches.en: THE CHANGE: a future identity is spoken of as already true.
branches.cn: 变化线：未来的身份被说成已经成立。

branches.en: THE GRAMMAR: the same verb carries other actions through time and into the passive.
branches.cn: 语法线：同一个动词把别的动作带过时间，并带进被动语态。

intro.en: Be is a root verb rather than a derived word; its family comes from merged forms and compounds like maybe.

definition_zh: 海滩；沙滩；海滨；使（船）搁浅
definition_en: an area of sand or small stones along the edge of the sea or a lake
core_image: 一条浅色的沙滩沿着海水弯过去
scene: 夏天，一家人带着遮阳伞和桶来到海边，在沙地上铺开毯子。We spent the whole afternoon on the beach.
sceneCN: 这里 beach 是「海滩」（第 1 个义项：海边的沙地）；句意为我们整个下午都待在海滩上。

pos.zh: 动词：使（船）搁浅；把……拖上岸

senses.title: Sandy ground by water
senses.definition: a stretch of sand or small stones beside the sea or a lake
senses.definitionCN: 海边或湖边的一片沙地或小石子地
senses.example: We spent the whole afternoon on the beach.
senses.exampleCN: 我们整个下午都待在海滩上。
senses.why: The old word meant the loose stones and sand washed up by water, so the ground itself is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个古词本指被水冲上来的松散沙石，所以那片地面本身是第一义。

senses.title: The seaside as a place
senses.definition: the seaside area as a place people visit for holidays
senses.definitionCN: 作为度假去处被人们前往的海边地区
senses.example: They go to the beach every summer.
senses.exampleCN: 他们每年夏天都去海边。
senses.why: The ground became a destination, so the word can name the whole holiday place rather than only the sand.
senses.whyCN: 那片地面成了目的地，于是这个词能指整个度假去处，而不只是沙地。

senses.title: To run a boat aground
senses.definition: to pull a boat up onto the shore, or to come to rest on the shore unintentionally
senses.definitionCN: 把船拖上岸，或船意外地停在岸边
senses.example: The storm beached the small boat on the sand.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴把那只小船搁上了沙滩。
senses.why: The verb is the shore in action: moving a boat from the water onto that very ground.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是那片岸地在起作用：把船从水里移到那片地面上去。

intro.en: Beach is an Old English word for the shore, and its oldest recorded meaning was the pebbles washed up by the sea.
intro.cn: beach 是古英语中表示岸的词，最早记录的意思是海水冲上来的小石子。

items.en: Bæce first meant the loose stones or gravel washed up by the sea.
items.cn: bæce 最初指海水冲上来的散石或砾石。

items.en: Related words for a stream or a bank occur in other Germanic languages; the exact link is not settled.
items.cn: 其他日耳曼语中有表示溪流或岸的相关词，具体联系尚未定论。

items.en: The meaning widened from loose stones to the whole sandy shore.
items.cn: 词义从「散石」扩展到整片沙质的岸边。

items.en: The holiday sense of the seaside grows as travel to the coast becomes common.
items.cn: 随着去海边旅行变得普遍，「海滨度假地」这一义项逐渐形成。

items.en: The verb beached, used of boats stuck on the shore, comes from the noun.
items.cn: 动词 beached 指船停在岸上，是由名词发展出来的。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds and forms built on beach; the near-meaning group gathers other words for shores and for running aground.
note.cn: 形近组收由 beach 构成的复合词与形式；近义组收表示岸边与搁浅的其他词。

entries.definition: The land along the edge of any large body of water; broader than beach.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「岸」，范围比 beach 更广，可指任何大水域的边缘。

entries.definition: The land beside the sea seen as a long line, often on a map.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「海岸」，常指地图上的整条海岸线。

entries.definition: The loose grains that cover many beaches.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「沙子」，是许多海滩的覆盖物。

entries.definition: A shore, or to leave something stuck on a shore; literary in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「岸；使搁浅」，文学色彩较浓。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real pebble origin of the word, its compounds, and the fixed phrases it appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用这个词真实的「卵石」来源、复合词，以及它的固定搭配。

normal.en: The oldest sense was the pebbles washed up by the sea, which is why a beach can be stony rather than sandy.
normal.cn: 最早的意思是海水冲上来的卵石，所以海滩也可能是石子滩而不是沙滩。

normal.en: On the beach keeps the prepositions fixed: you are on it, not in it.
normal.cn: on the beach 的介词是固定的：人在它「上面」，不在「里面」。

normal.en: Beach towel, beach ball, and beach umbrella are all objects brought to the shore.
normal.cn: beach towel、beach ball、beach umbrella 都是带到岸边的物件。

normal.en: A beached whale is one that has come to rest on the shore.
normal.cn: beached whale 指一头停在岸上的鲸。

normal.en: The verb beach moves a boat from water to sand, which is the noun turned into an action.
normal.cn: 动词 beach 把船从水里移到沙上，就是名词变成了动作。

abstract.en: Picture a pale strip of sand curving along blue water, with the edge changing twice a day.
abstract.cn: 想象一条浅色沙带沿着蓝色的水弯过去，它的边缘一天变换两次。

abstract.en: The beach is not fixed: the tide builds it and takes it away, which is why the word began with loose stones.
abstract.cn: 海滩并不固定：潮水造出它又带走它，所以这个词最初与散石有关。

abstract.en: A place of rest and a place of shipwreck share one word, because both are where water meets land.
abstract.cn: 休息之地与失事之地共用一个词，因为两者都是水与陆相遇之处。

definition_zh: 豆；豆子；豆类植物；咖啡豆
definition_en: a seed of a climbing plant, used as food, or a seed that looks like it
core_image: 一把圆鼓鼓的豆子泡在清水里，慢慢涨大
scene: 做饭前，她把一杯干豆子倒进碗里，用水泡了一夜。She soaked a cup of beans before making soup.
sceneCN: 这里 bean 是「豆子」（第 1 个义项：可食用的豆类种子）；句意为她做汤前泡了一杯豆子。

pos.zh: 名词：豆；豆子；豆类植物；咖啡豆

senses.title: An edible seed
senses.definition: a seed from a climbing plant, cooked and eaten as food
senses.definitionCN: 藤本植物结出的种子，煮熟后作为食物
senses.example: She soaked a cup of beans before making soup.
senses.exampleCN: 她做汤前泡了一杯豆子。
senses.why: The word has named the edible seed since Old English, so the food itself is the centre.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从古英语起就指可食用的种子，所以食物本身是中心义。

senses.title: The plant that bears them
senses.definition: the plant that produces these seeds, often grown in fields
senses.definitionCN: 结出这种种子的植物，常在田里成片种植
senses.example: Farmers plant beans in spring and harvest them in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 农民春天种豆，夏天收获。
senses.why: As with many crops, the seed's name also names the plant that carries it.
senses.whyCN: 和许多作物一样，种子的名字也用来指结出它的植物。

senses.title: A seed of another plant
senses.definition: a seed of a different plant that looks like a bean, especially a coffee bean
senses.definitionCN: 外形像豆子的其他植物种子，尤指咖啡豆
senses.example: These coffee beans come from a small farm.
senses.exampleCN: 这些咖啡豆来自一个小农场。
senses.why: The shape is the link: any small oval seed can borrow the name of the familiar food.
senses.whyCN: 联系在形状：任何椭圆形的小种子都能借用这种熟悉食物的名字。

senses.title: A small amount, in negative phrases
senses.definition: a very small amount, used in phrases such as not know beans
senses.definitionCN: 极少的量，用于 not know beans 这类说法
senses.example: He does not know beans about fixing bikes.
senses.exampleCN: 他对修自行车一窍不通。
senses.why: A bean is small and cheap, so in negative phrases it stands for something almost worthless.
senses.whyCN: 豆子又小又便宜，所以在否定说法里它代表几乎不值一提的东西。

senses.title: Energy, in full of beans
senses.definition: in the phrase full of beans, full of energy and high spirits
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 full of beans，指精力旺盛、兴致很高
senses.example: The children were full of beans after the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 旅行回来后孩子们精力充沛。
senses.why: Beans are solid, nourishing food, so a person full of them is pictured as full of energy.
senses.whyCN: 豆子是实在而有营养的食物，所以「装满豆子」的人就被想象成充满精力。

intro.en: Bean is an old Germanic word, and a related Latin word for the same plant survives as faba.
intro.cn: bean 是古老的日耳曼语词，拉丁语中表示同一种植物的相关词是 faba。

items.en: A reconstructed root for the bean plant lies behind both the Germanic and the Latin words.
items.cn: 一个可重构、指豆类植物的词根，是日耳曼语词与拉丁语词共同的远源。

items.en: Old English bean meant the edible seed, and the word kept that meaning without a break.
items.cn: 古英语 bean 指可食用的种子，这个词一直保留着这个意思。

items.en: Related forms in other Germanic languages confirm the shape of the old root.
items.cn: 其他日耳曼语中的相关形式印证了这一古老词根的形态。

items.en: English applied the word to coffee beans and other small oval seeds.
items.cn: 英语把这个词用到咖啡豆和其他椭圆形小种子上。

items.en: Informal phrases such as full of beans and not know beans add the later senses.
items.cn: full of beans 与 not know beans 这类口语说法带来了较晚的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on bean; the near-meaning group gathers other seeds and pulses.
note.cn: 形近组收由 bean 构成的词；近义组收其他种子与豆类。

entries.definition: A small flat seed cooked in soups and stews.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小扁豆」，扁平小粒，常煮汤。

entries.definition: The general word for the part of a plant that can grow into a new plant.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「种子」，是这类可繁殖部分的总称。

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「咖啡」，指烤过的豆子做成的饮品，而非种子本身。

normal.en: Bean has meant the edible seed since Old English, so the food sense is the oldest.

normal.en: A beanstalk is what Jack climbed, and a beanpole is what the stalk grows on.
normal.cn: beanstalk 是杰克爬过的豆茎，beanpole 则是豆茎攀爬的支架。

normal.en: Coffee beans look like beans, which is why the shape gave them the name.

normal.en: Not know beans means to know nothing, because a bean is worth very little.
normal.cn: not know beans 意为一无所知，因为一颗豆子值不了什么。

abstract.en: Picture a dry bean in water: it swells quietly overnight, and that small change is the start of a meal.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗干豆泡在水里：一夜之间悄悄涨大，这点变化就是一顿饭的开始。

abstract.en: One seed holds a whole plant inside, which is why the same word names seed and plant.
abstract.cn: 一颗种子里面藏着一整株植物，所以同一个词既指种子也指植物。

abstract.en: Cheap, small, and nourishing, the bean becomes a picture of both energy and worthlessness in English phrases.

senses.title: To hit again and again
senses.definition: to hit something many times with force
senses.definitionCN: 用力反复击打某物
senses.example: He beat the drum during the parade.

senses.why: The Old English verb meant to strike, so repeated striking is the oldest and most physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个古英语动词本义就是「击打」，所以反复击打是最古老、最具体的义项。

senses.title: To defeat
senses.definition: to win against someone in a game, fight, or competition
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、打斗或竞争中胜过对方
senses.example: Our team beat the other class in the final match.
senses.exampleCN: 我们队在决赛中战胜了另一个班。
senses.why: A fight is a series of blows, and the one still standing has beaten the other, so striking grows into defeating.
senses.whyCN: 打斗是一连串的击打，还站着的一方就「打」赢了对方，于是「击打」长成了「击败」。

senses.title: To mix food quickly
senses.definition: to mix eggs, cream, or batter quickly with a fork or machine
senses.definitionCN: 用叉子或机器快速搅拌鸡蛋、奶油或面糊
senses.example: Beat the eggs before you add the milk.
senses.exampleCN: 加牛奶之前先把鸡蛋打散。
senses.why: Rapid stirring is a kind of repeated striking against the mixture, so the same verb serves the kitchen.
senses.whyCN: 快速搅拌就是对混合物反复击打，所以同一个动词也进了厨房。

senses.title: A regular rhythm
senses.definition: the regular strong pulse in music or in a poem
senses.definitionCN: 音乐或诗歌中规律出现的强拍
senses.example: The drummer kept a steady beat for the whole song.
senses.exampleCN: 鼓手整首歌都保持着稳定的节拍。
senses.why: A drum is struck again and again at equal intervals, and the pattern of strikes becomes the beat.
senses.whyCN: 鼓被等间隔地反复敲击，这些敲击形成的规律就成了「节拍」。

senses.title: To pulse
senses.definition: to move or sound with a regular pulse, as the heart does
senses.definitionCN: 像心脏那样规律地跳动或发出声响
senses.example: Her heart beat fast after the race.
senses.exampleCN: 赛跑之后她的心跳得很快。
senses.why: The heart strikes the chest from inside with a regular rhythm, so the verb moves from drum to body.
senses.whyCN: 心脏在胸腔里规律地撞击，于是这个动词从鼓面移到了身体上。

intro.en: Beat is a native English verb with a Germanic root and a strong, irregular past form.
intro.cn: beat 是本族英语动词，源于日耳曼语，过去式与过去分词为不规则的强变化形式。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning to strike lies behind the Germanic verb.
items.cn: 一个可重构、意为「击打」的词根，是这一日耳曼语动词的远源。

items.en: The Germanic verb bautan meant to beat or to strike.
items.cn: 日耳曼语动词 bautan 意为「打、击」。

items.en: Old English beatan meant to strike repeatedly, and it kept a strong past participle.
items.cn: 古英语 beatan 意为「反复击打」，并保留了强变化的过去分词。

items.en: The sense of defeating an opponent grows from the image of a fight.
items.cn: 「击败对手」的义项从打斗的意象中发展出来。

items.en: Music and the heart give the noun its sense of a regular pulse.
items.cn: 音乐与心脏赋予名词「规律搏动」的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms and derivatives of the verb; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs for striking and winning.
note.cn: 形近组收这个动词的形式与派生词；近义组收表示击打与获胜的其他动词。

entries.definition: The past participle, also used as an adjective meaning defeated or worn by blows.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词，也作形容词，义为「被打败的、被敲打的」。

entries.definition: The act of striking, or a regular pulsing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「敲打；搏动」，由 beat 加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: A tool or person that beats, such as an egg beater.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「搅拌器；敲打者」，如打蛋器。

entries.definition: A root vegetable; it sounds the same but comes from a different Latin word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「甜菜」；读音相同，但词源来自另一个拉丁词，与 beat 无关。

entries.definition: To strike once; it does not suggest repetition like beat.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「打、击中」，通常指一次，而不像 beat 强调反复。

entries.definition: To hit with force, often once and deliberately.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「击、打」，常指一次有意的重击。

entries.definition: To win against someone; the formal word for the second sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「击败」，是第二个义项的正式说法。

entries.definition: A regular pattern of sounds; it is close to the noun sense of beat.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「节奏」，与 beat 的名词义接近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real strong forms beat and beaten, the suffixes, and the fixed phrases with beat.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的强变化形式 beat 与 beaten、后缀，以及 beat 的固定搭配。

normal.en: The past tense is beat and the past participle is beaten, so the verb keeps an old strong pattern.
normal.cn: 过去式是 beat，过去分词是 beaten，这个动词保留了古老的强变化模式。

normal.en: Beat the drum is the literal action that gave the word its musical sense.
normal.cn: beat the drum 正是赋予这个词音乐义的字面动作。

normal.en: Beat eggs means stir them hard, as if striking them again and again.
normal.cn: beat eggs 意为用力搅打，好像反复击打它们。

normal.en: Unbeaten means no one has ever beaten that team.
normal.cn: unbeaten 意为从未有队伍击败过它。

normal.en: Beat about the bush means going around the point instead of hitting it directly.
normal.cn: beat about the bush 意为绕着话题走，而不直接点中要害。

abstract.en: Picture a drum skin: each blow fades fast, but the next one comes at the same distance, and that spacing is rhythm.
abstract.cn: 想象一张鼓面：每一下很快消失，但下一下总在同样的间隔到来，这个间隔就是节奏。

abstract.en: A fight and a football match share one verb, because both end when one side can no longer answer.
abstract.cn: 打斗与足球赛共用一个动词，因为两者都在一方无法回应时结束。

abstract.en: The heart does the drummer's work without a drummer, which is why the same word covers music and pulse.
abstract.cn: 心脏在没有鼓手的情况下做着鼓手的事，所以同一个词既指音乐也指脉搏。

examples.en: Our team beat the other class in the final match.
examples.cn: 我们队在决赛中战胜了另一个班。

examples.en: He beat the drum during the parade.
examples.cn: 游行时他敲着鼓。

examples.en: Her heart beat fast after the race.
examples.cn: 赛跑之后她的心跳得很快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「必特」——鼓点必特别准，一下一下打在节拍上：敲打、节拍

root: beat 来自古英语 beatan「反复击打」，源于日耳曼语 bautan，可上溯到原始印欧语中意为「击打」的重构词根。由「击打」引申出「击败」「搅打」，又由鼓的反复敲击引申出名词「节拍」与「心跳」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of beat all come from repeated striking: hitting, defeating, stirring food, the pattern of drum strikes, and the pulse of the heart.
sensesIntro.cn: beat 的五个义项都来自反复击打：打、击败、搅打食物、鼓点的规律，以及心脏的搏动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drumstick falls on the skin again and again at equal intervals.
core.cn: 核心意象：鼓槌一下一下，以相等的间隔落在鼓面上。

branches.en: THE STRIKE: the oldest sense is plain repeated hitting.
branches.cn: 击打线：最古老的义项就是单纯反复地打。

branches.en: THE FIGHT: the side that keeps striking wins, so hitting becomes defeating.
branches.cn: 胜负线：还能继续打的一方获胜，于是「打」变成「击败」。

branches.en: THE KITCHEN: fast stirring is striking the mixture again and again.
branches.cn: 厨房线：快速搅拌就是反复击打混合物。

branches.en: THE PATTERN: equal spacing between drum strikes becomes musical beat.
branches.cn: 规律线：鼓击之间相等的间隔成了音乐的节拍。

branches.en: THE BODY: the heart repeats the drummer's action inside the chest.
branches.cn: 身体线：心脏在胸腔里重复着鼓手的动作。

intro.en: Beat is a strong Germanic verb, so it marks tense by changing its vowel rather than adding -ed.
intro.cn: beat 是日耳曼语强变化动词，靠改变元音而非加 -ed 来表示时态。

latinIntro.en: Latin battuere also meant to beat, but it is a separate root and not a cognate, so no Latin entry is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 battuere 也意为「打」，但那是另一个词根，并非同族词，因此不列拉丁词条。

items.exampleCN: 他用拳头捶门。

它构成 beaten。
它构成 beating。

items.meaning: a person or tool that does
items.exampleCN: 它构成 beater。

definition_zh: 美丽的；漂亮的；美好的；出色的
definition_en: very pleasing to look at, hear, or think about
core_image: 湖面上浮着薄雾，岸边的花在晨光里开满
scene: 清晨的湖面浮着一层薄雾，岸边的花在光里显得格外好看。The lake looks beautiful in the early morning light.
sceneCN: 这里 beautiful 是「美丽的」（第 1 个义项：外表令人愉悦）；句意为清晨的光线下这座湖显得很美。

pos.zh: 形容词：美丽的；漂亮的；美好的；出色的

derivatives.zh: 基础名词，义为「美；美人」，beautiful 由它加后缀构成
由 beautiful 加 -ly 构成，义为「美丽地；出色地」
由 beauty 加 -ify 构成，义为「使变美；美化」
由 beauty 加 -ician 构成，义为「美容师」

senses.title: Pleasing to look at
senses.definition: very attractive to the eye, as a person, place, or object
senses.definitionCN: 在视觉上非常吸引人，如人、地方或物品
senses.example: The lake looks beautiful in the early morning light.
senses.exampleCN: 清晨的光线下这座湖显得很美。
senses.why: Beauty first names the quality that pleases the eye, so the visual sense is the base of the word.
senses.whyCN: beauty 最初指取悦眼睛的性质，所以视觉义是这个词的基础。

senses.title: Pleasing to hear
senses.definition: very pleasing to the ear, as music or a voice
senses.definitionCN: 在听觉上非常悦耳，如音乐或嗓音
senses.example: She has a beautiful singing voice.
senses.exampleCN: 她的歌声很美。
senses.why: The eye's pleasure extends to the ear, because both judge a pattern as harmonious.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛的愉悦扩展到耳朵，因为两者都在判断一种和谐的形式。

senses.title: Good and kind
senses.definition: morally good, generous, or touching in behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 在行为上善良、慷慨或令人感动
senses.example: It was a beautiful act of kindness.
senses.exampleCN: 那是一个美好的善举。
senses.why: Inner goodness is felt as a kind of beauty, so the word also praises the heart.
senses.whyCN: 内在的善良被感受为一种美，所以这个词也用来称赞心地。

senses.title: Excellent, informally
senses.definition: used informally to praise a skill or a result as very good
senses.definitionCN: 口语中用来称赞某项技能或结果非常好
senses.example: That was a beautiful shot!
senses.exampleCN: 那一脚射门太漂亮了！
senses.why: A perfect action has the same rightness as a beautiful object, so informal speech uses the word for skill.
senses.whyCN: 完美的动作与美的物体有同样的「恰到好处」，所以口语用这个词称赞技艺。

intro.en: Beautiful is English beauty plus the suffix -ful, and beauty came from Latin through French.
intro.cn: beautiful 是英语 beauty 加后缀 -ful 构成，而 beauty 经法语来自拉丁语。

items.en: Latin bellus meant pretty or fine, probably from a small form of bonus, good.
items.cn: 拉丁语 bellus 意为「漂亮的、美好的」，可能来自 bonus「好」的小称形式。

items.en: Spoken Latin formed a noun for the quality of being bellus.
items.cn: 通俗拉丁语为「美的性质」造了一个名词。

items.en: Old French beauté carried the noun into English as beauty.
items.cn: 古法语 beauté 把这个名词以 beauty 的形式带入英语。

items.en: English beauty is recorded from the Middle Ages and names the quality itself.
items.cn: 英语 beauty 自中世纪起有记录，指美这种性质本身。

items.en: The adjective beautiful adds -ful, meaning full of, so it describes something full of beauty.
items.cn: 形容词 beautiful 加上 -ful「充满」，表示「充满美的」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the beauty family; the near-meaning group gathers other words for attractiveness and excellence.
note.cn: 形近组收 beauty 词族；近义组收表示吸引力与出色的其他词。

entries.definition: The quality of being beautiful, or a beautiful person or thing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「美；美人、美物」，是 beautiful 的基础词。

entries.definition: Adverb meaning in a beautiful way or very well.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「美丽地；出色地」，由 beautiful 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: To make something beautiful.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使变美、美化」，由 beauty 加 -ify 构成。

entries.definition: A person whose job is to improve other people's appearance.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「美容师」，由 beauty 加 -ician 构成。

entries.definition: Attractive in a light, pleasant way; often softer than beautiful.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「漂亮的」，语气比 beautiful 更轻、更日常。

entries.definition: Pleasing and warm; it can describe people, weather, or a time.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可爱的、美好的」，可形容人、天气或时光。

entries.definition: Extremely beautiful; stronger and more informal than beautiful.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「极美的」，比 beautiful 更强、更口语。

entries.definition: Pleasing enough to draw attention; less emotional than beautiful.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有吸引力的」，比 beautiful 更中性、更少情感色彩。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real beauty root, the suffix -ful, and the family words built with -ly, -ify and -ician.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的 beauty 词根、后缀 -ful，以及由 -ly、-ify、-ician 构成的词族。

normal.en: Beautiful is beauty plus -ful, so it literally means full of beauty.
normal.cn: beautiful 是 beauty 加 -ful，字面意思就是「充满美的」。

normal.en: Beauty came from French beauté, which came from Latin bellus, pretty.
normal.cn: beauty 来自法语 beauté，再往前是拉丁语 bellus「漂亮的」。

normal.en: Beautifully adds -ly and describes how something is done, not what it is.
normal.cn: beautifully 加 -ly，描述事情做得如何，而不是事物本身如何。

normal.en: Beautify means to make beautiful, and beautician names the person who does it.
normal.cn: beautify 意为使变美，beautician 指做这件事的人。

normal.en: Long adjectives take more and most: more beautiful, most beautiful.
normal.cn: 多音节形容词用 more 与 most：more beautiful、most beautiful。

abstract.en: Picture a still lake at dawn: nothing is added, yet the whole scene feels complete.
abstract.cn: 想象黎明时静止的湖面：没有增添什么，整个景象却显得完整。

abstract.en: The word begins with the eye but reaches the ear, the heart, and even a good football shot.
abstract.cn: 这个词从眼睛出发，却抵达耳朵、内心，甚至一脚漂亮的射门。

abstract.en: Beauty is not a thing but a relation between a pattern and the person who sees it.
abstract.cn: 美不是一件东西，而是形式与观看者之间的一种关系。

examples.en: The lake looks beautiful in the early morning light.
examples.cn: 清晨的光线下这座湖显得很美。

examples.en: She has a beautiful singing voice.
examples.cn: 她的歌声很美。

examples.en: It was a beautiful act of kindness.
examples.cn: 那是一个美好的善举。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「标体否」——身材标致，谁能否认：美丽的

root: beautiful 由 beauty 加后缀 -ful「充满」构成。beauty 经古法语 beauté 来自通俗拉丁语，源头为拉丁语 bellus「漂亮的、美好的」，bellus 可能出自 bonus「好」的小称形式。词义由视觉之美扩展到听觉、品德与技艺。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of beautiful widen the idea of beauty: what pleases the eye, what pleases the ear, what is good in the heart, and what is done with excellence.
sensesIntro.cn: beautiful 的四个义项不断拓宽「美」：悦目、悦耳、心地善良，以及做得极为出色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a calm lake at dawn with flowers along the shore.
core.cn: 核心意象：黎明时平静的湖面，岸边开满花。

branches.en: THE SIGHT: the first sense is what pleases the eye.
branches.cn: 视觉线：第一义是取悦眼睛之物。

branches.en: THE SOUND: the same harmony is heard in music and voices.
branches.cn: 听觉线：同样的和谐在音乐与嗓音中被听见。

branches.en: THE HEART: inner goodness is felt as beauty too.
branches.cn: 内心线：内在的善良也被感受为美。

branches.en: THE SKILL: a perfect action has the rightness of a beautiful object.
branches.cn: 技艺线：完美的动作与美的物体同样恰到好处。

branches.en: THE WHOLENESS: beauty is a pattern that feels complete, whether seen or done.
branches.cn: 整体线：美是一种显得完整的形式，无论被看见还是被做出。

intro.en: Beautiful is a Latin-derived noun with the English suffix -ful, and it forms a large family.
intro.cn: beautiful 是拉丁来源的名词加英语后缀 -ful，并形成一个较大的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin bellus and the later noun bellitas are recorded and are the source of beauty.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 bellus 与后来的名词 bellitas 均有记录，是 beauty 的来源。

items.exampleCN: 这个地方的美让我们吃惊。

definition_zh: 美丽地；优美地；出色地
definition_en: in a beautiful way, or very well
core_image: 舞台的灯光落在舞者身上，动作轻而准确
scene: 学校演出时，她在台上跳完一支舞，动作又轻又准。She danced beautifully at the school show.
sceneCN: 这里 beautifully 是「优美地」（第 1 个义项：以美丽动人的方式）；句意为她在学校演出上跳得很优美。

pos.zh: 副词：美丽地；优美地；出色地

senses.title: In a beautiful way
senses.definition: in a way that is beautiful to see or hear
senses.definitionCN: 以看起来或听起来很美的方式
senses.example: She danced beautifully at the school show.
senses.exampleCN: 她在学校演出上跳得很优美。
senses.why: The suffix -ly turns the adjective beautiful into the manner of an action, so the first sense describes how something is done.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ly 把形容词 beautiful 变成动作的方式，所以第一义描述事情做得如何。

senses.title: Very well
senses.definition: in a very skillful or excellent way
senses.definitionCN: 以非常熟练或出色的方式
senses.example: He played the piano beautifully.
senses.exampleCN: 他钢琴弹得很出色。
senses.why: An action done perfectly looks as right as a beautiful object, so the word also praises skill.
senses.whyCN: 做得完美的动作与美的物体一样恰到好处，所以这个词也用来称赞技艺。

intro.en: Beautifully is beautiful plus the old adverb suffix -ly, and its root reaches back to Latin bellus.
intro.cn: beautifully 是 beautiful 加古老的副词后缀 -ly，词根可上溯到拉丁语 bellus。

items.en: Latin bellus meant pretty or fine, probably from a small form of bonus, good.
items.cn: 拉丁语 bellus 意为「漂亮的、美好的」，可能来自 bonus「好」的小称形式。

items.en: The noun for beauty passed through Old French into English as beauty.
items.cn: 表示「美」的名词经古法语以 beauty 进入英语。

items.en: English formed the adjective beautiful by adding -ful to beauty.
items.cn: 英语给 beauty 加上 -ful，构成了形容词 beautiful。

items.en: The adverb suffix -ly goes back to Old English -lice, meaning in the manner of.
items.cn: 副词后缀 -ly 可追溯到古英语 -lice，意为「以……的方式」。

items.en: Beautifully is recorded from the later Middle English period; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: beautifully 在中古英语后期已有记录，确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the beauty family; the near-meaning group gathers other adverbs of manner and praise.
note.cn: 形近组收 beauty 词族；近义组收其他方式副词与称赞用语。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning very pleasing to see or hear.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「美丽的、优美的」，是 beautifully 的基础词。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being beautiful.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「美」，是这个词族的根名词。

entries.definition: To make something beautiful.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「美化、使变美」。

entries.definition: In a dutiful way; it shares the -ful plus -ly ending but not the root.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「尽职地」，词尾同样是 -ful 加 -ly，但词根不同。

entries.definition: In a good or skillful way; the plain word for the second sense.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「好、很好地」，是第二个义项最朴素的说法。

entries.definition: With smooth, elegant movement; close to the first sense for bodies.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「优雅地」，形容动作流畅，接近第一义用于身体时的意思。

entries.definition: In a magnificent or excellent way; stronger and more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「壮丽地、极好地」，语气更强也更正式。

entries.definition: In a way that has no faults; it stresses accuracy rather than beauty.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「完美地」，强调没有差错，而不强调美感。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real pieces of the word: beautiful plus -ly, and the family behind it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用这个词的真实构件：beautiful 加 -ly，以及它背后的词族。

normal.en: Beautiful plus -ly describes the manner, so danced beautifully tells how she danced.
normal.cn: beautiful 加 -ly 描述方式，所以 danced beautifully 说明她跳得怎样。

normal.en: The adverb never compares beauty itself; it only says an action was done in that way.
normal.cn: 这个副词并不比较美本身，只说明动作是以那种方式完成的。

normal.en: Beau-ti-ful-ly has four beats, and the stress stays on the first syllable.
normal.cn: beau-ti-ful-ly 有四个音节，重音仍在第一个音节上。

normal.en: Beautifully made and beautifully written describe the result of careful work.
normal.cn: beautifully made 与 beautifully written 都形容用心做出来的结果。

normal.en: Played beautifully means played very well, which is the second sense.
normal.cn: played beautifully 意为弹得很好，正是第二个义项。

abstract.en: Picture a dancer finishing a turn and holding still: the stillness is as important as the movement.
abstract.cn: 想象舞者转完一圈后定住：那份静止与动作本身同样重要。

abstract.en: An adverb does not change the thing; it changes the way we see the thing being done.
abstract.cn: 副词不改变事物本身，只改变我们看待那件事如何被完成的方式。

abstract.en: The same word praises a dance, a sentence, and a well-made chair, because all three feel finished.
abstract.cn: 同一个词能称赞一支舞、一句话和一把做得很好的椅子，因为三者都显得完整。

examples.en: She danced beautifully at the school show.
examples.cn: 她在学校演出上跳得很优美。

examples.en: He played the piano beautifully.
examples.cn: 他钢琴弹得很出色。

examples.en: The little garden is beautifully simple.
examples.cn: 这个小花园简洁而美。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「标体否离」——标致的身形离不开优美的动作：优美地

root: beautifully 由 beautiful 加副词后缀 -ly 构成；-ly 来自古英语 -lice「以……方式」。beautiful 由 beauty 加 -ful「充满」构成，beauty 经古法语 beauté 上溯到拉丁语 bellus「漂亮的」。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses of beautifully share one manner: doing something in a way that pleases, whether the pleasure is beauty or sheer skill.
sensesIntro.cn: beautifully 的两个义项共用一种「方式」：以令人愉悦的方式完成某事，愉悦可以来自美感，也可以来自纯熟的技艺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dancer holds a perfect line under a single light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束灯光下，舞者定出一个完美的线条。

branches.en: THE MANNER: the suffix -ly makes the word describe how an action is done.
branches.cn: 方式线：后缀 -ly 让这个词描述动作是怎样完成的。

branches.en: THE BEAUTY: the action itself is pleasing to watch or hear.
branches.cn: 美感线：动作本身看起来或听起来令人愉悦。

branches.en: THE SKILL: a perfectly done action earns the same word as a beautiful object.
branches.cn: 技艺线：完成得完美的动作，与美的物体得到同一个词。

branches.en: THE CARE: beautifully made things show steady, careful work.
branches.cn: 用心线：做得精美的东西显出稳定而细致的工夫。

branches.en: THE RESULT: the word often appears beside made, written, and played.
branches.cn: 结果线：这个词常与 made、written、played 连用。

intro.en: Beautifully is a transparent formation: a Latin-derived adjective plus the English adverb suffix -ly.
intro.cn: beautifully 是结构透明的构词：拉丁来源的形容词加英语副词后缀 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Latin bellus and Late Latin bellitas are recorded and lie behind the beauty family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 bellus 与晚期拉丁语 bellitas 均有记录，是 beauty 词族的来源。

items.example: The beauty of the song moved us.
items.exampleCN: 这首歌的美打动了我们。
它构成 beautiful。

items.meaning: very pleasing to see or hear
items.exampleCN: 那景色很美。
它构成 beautifully。

items.meaning: in a beautiful or skillful way
items.exampleCN: 她唱得很美。
它由 beauty 构成 beautify。
它构成 beautician。
它与 beautifully 构成比较级。
